ment to the more promising
junior members of the staff,
to encourage efficiency, and at
the same time to effect econom-
ies; the results of this reorgan-
ization may not be apparent to
the public for a little time.
6.—Steps have been taken
gradually to make way for the
greater employment of capable
Chinese in the Municipal service.
7.—A Salaries Commission
has been appointed and is now
sitting to go into the question
of salaries generally and make
recommendations to the Council.
8.—A Staff Association has
been formed with a view to
harmonising the relations be-
tween the Council and the
staff.
9.—The whole of the Council's
educational system is in process
of reorganization to provide for
the equal distribution of the
Council's educational facilities
between the foreign and Chinese
communities, thus removing a
great source of grievance to the
Chinese population of the Settle-
ment. This reorganization,
whilst effecting very consider-
able economy and giving direc-
tion to the Council's educational
policy, will not only effect
economies but will increase the
efficiency of the schools, which
are now being placed under a
permanent Board of Education
in conjunction with a Supervisor
of Schools.
There is a great deal more to
be done to complete all this work,
but I can leave it to the public to
decide whether the mandate,
which I was given, has been
persistently carried out, or not.
In July last year urgent com-
plaints were received from the
various chambers of commerce
and ratepayers with regard to the
way in which it is faced, by appointing
one or more persons of inter-
national reputation to come here
and study the situation and advise
them. Thanks to Mr. Fessenden's
tact and able handling of the
situation whilst he was in Kyoto,
a far better understanding and
more sympathetic attitude to-
wards the problems with which
Shanghai is faced, has resulted,
both in England and in America.
These are surely no barren re-
sults to show for the year's work?
Since, however, the electorate by
its decision, as shown in the
election, has not endorsed the
policy pursued, I obviously cannot,
without embarrassing the present
Council, give any guidance with
regard to the policy for the forth-
coming year, which will, during
the next few weeks, have to re-
ceive consideration. I, therefore,
felt that my continued presence
on the Council would only be a
cause for embarrassment, and
have resigned, although in taking
this step I have deprived myself
of the opportunity of addressing
the ratepayers and submitting an
account of my stewardship for the
past year.
Before closing I would refer
briefly to the disloyal letter, which
one of your contemporaries
published prior to the election. I
was unable to reply so long as I
remained Chairman of the Council
without committing a breach of
the rules, which were confirmed
during the period when Mr. Bell
was Vice-Chairman, and which
specifically laid down that no
member of the Council may dis-
close or discuss in public, whilst
still a member of the Council, any
divergent opinion from the Council
as a whole. Most statements in
that letter are, to say the least,
misleading, but I will confine my-
self to stating that public life in
Shanghai is rapidly degenerating,
when a newspaper of standing
prints and describes as "courage-
ous" the fact that a member of
the Council has broken faith with
his colleagues—a member who
has stated in that letter that he
favours admitting the public to
the deliberations of the Council,
although, to the best of my re-
collection, he has not thought fit
to raise this subject in the
Council Chamber.
H. ARNHOLD.
Shanghai, March 6, 1930

要完成所有这些工作还有很多事情要做，但我可以让公众来决定，我所获得的授权是否得到了坚持不懈的执行。
去年七月，各商会和纳税人就面对的方式提出了紧急投诉，通过任命一名或多名具有国际声誉的人士前来研究局势并提供建议。多亏费森登先生在京都期间机智且得力地处理局势，在英国和美国都产生了更好的理解以及对上海所面临问题的更同情态度。

然而，既然选民通过选举所示的决定并未认可所执行的政策，我显然不能在不使现任董事会尴尬的情况下，对来年即将在未来几周内加以考虑的政策提供任何指导。因此，我觉得我继续留在董事会只会造成尴尬，故已辞职，尽管采取这一步骤使我失去了向纳税人致辞并提交过去一年履职报告的机会。
在结束之前，我想简要提及贵报同行之一在选举前发表的那封不忠信件。只要我仍担任董事会主席，我就无法回复，否则将违反规则，这些规则是在贝尔先生（Mr. Bell）担任副主席期间确认的，并明确规定董事会任何成员在仍是董事会成员期间，不得公开披露或讨论与董事会整体存在的任何分歧意见。那封信中的大多数陈述至少具有误导性，但我仅局限于指出，当一家有地位的报纸刊登并将一名董事会成员违背对其同事的承诺描述为“勇敢”时，上海的公共生活正在迅速堕落——该成员在那封信中表示他赞成允许公众参与董事会的审议，尽管据我回忆，他认为不宜在董事会会议室提出此议题。

H. 安诺德
上海，1930年3月6日

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, MARCH 7, 1930

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. I. O. D. 1043
Date..7.....3 - 30

Reasons For Resigning
Given In Statement By
Late Council Chairman

H. E. Arnhold In Letter To THE CHINA PRESS
Outlines Reforms And Work Carried Out
During His Term Of Office

There is a lull in the storm caused by this year's surprise election for Municipal honors, and no further developments have taken place. The vacancy for chairmanship of the retiring council is being filled by Brig.-General E. B. Macnaghten, the vice-chairman, who will occupy this post until after the annual meeting of ratepayers which is to take place April 16.

In connection with his resignation at the special council meeting called last Wednesday evening, Mr. H. E. Arnhold has sent us the following letter for publication:

Editor, THE CHINA PRESS

Sir:—May I through your columns thank the 715 electors of this Community, representing more than half the votes recorded, who voted for me, for their support at the recent election and explain the reason for my resignation of the Chairmanship of the Council before termination of my period of office?

In view of the Leading Article in one of your contemporaries this morning and the reference to the controlling interest of the Japanese voters in the ultimate result, I feel it incumbent upon me to bring certain facts to the attention of the ratepayers, which it is in their interests to know.

As Chairman of the Council I have been unable to agree to certain requests which have been pressed upon me for what appeared to be a disproportionate increase in the Japanese Police and other matters, which could not be granted in their entirety. As a result of this, I was given to understand a few days prior to the election that I should only receive 200 out of the 600 Japanese votes. If this actually occurred, the Foreign Community must have supported me to the extent of 515 votes.

I understand that 90% of the Japanese electorate went to the Poll, as compared with about 50% of the British. It is therefore evident that so long as the British Community do not turn out in larger numbers to cast their vote, Municipal affairs will be controlled by the Japanese voting machine. Possibly, the Community may show more interest in Municipal affairs now that "new blood" has been infused into the Council "to shake it up."

May I, in this connection, remind you that a similar hope was expressed in the Press at the time of my election to the Council two years ago? The chief object for which I was asked to stand was to secure the carrying out of the recommendations of the Economy Committee. During the year of my tenure of office as Chairman, the following has, in that respect, been achieved:—

1. The Municipal Hospitals and Nursing System have been reorganized, resulting in greater efficiency and economy.

2. The Commissioner of Police has resigned and the services of a highly qualified police executive obtained from India to reorganise the Police Force, the reorganisation of which is now nearly completed.

3. Schemes have been evolved for the housing and improvement in the living conditions of both the Foreign and Chinese Police Force.

4. The Department of the Director of Chinese studies has been completely reorganized under a new and efficient hand, and the old system, which was found to be wasteful, has been discarded.

5. A Staff reorganization has been set in motion, with a view to cutting out dead wood in order to give more encouragement to the more promising junior members of the Staff, to encourage efficiency and at the same time to effect economies; the results of this reorganisation may not be apparent to the public for a little time.

6. Steps have been taken gradually to make way for the greater employment of capable Chinese in the Municipal service.

7. A Salaries Commission has been appointed and is now sitting to go into the question of Salaries generally and make recommendations to the Council.

8. A Staff Association has been formed, with a view to harmonizing the relations between the Council and the Staff.

9. The whole of the Council's Educational System is in process of reorganization to provide for the equal distribution of the Council's educational facilities between the Foreign and Chinese Communities, thus removing a great source of grievance to the Chinese population of the Settlement. This reorganization, whilst effecting very considerable economy and giving direction to the Council's educational policy, will not only effect economies but will increase the efficiency of the schools, which are now being placed under a permanent Board of Education in conjunction with a Supervisor of Schools.

There is a great deal more to be done to complete all this work, but I can leave it to the public to decide whether the mandate, which I was given, has been persistently carried out, or not.

TELEPHONE QUESTION

In July last year, urgent complaints were received from the various Chambers of Commerce and ratepayers with regard to the Telephone Service, pointing out that the Telephone Company had broken the terms of its franchise.

I felt very strongly that in view of the Council's responsibility in this respect, that it was imperative that the Council should obtain the service of an independent expert. The Telephone Company and the Council's nominee on the Board of Directors of that Company opposed this proposal on the ground that the expert's advice would serve no useful purpose, as the Company was committed to its present system. Mr. B. O. Anson, whose services were readily placed at the Council's disposal by the General Post Office, has presented his report, from which the public may judge very clearly the unsatisfactory state of the Telephone system and the drastic steps which are necessary for its rehabilitation. Two of the principal features of the report reveal that:

1. The Telephone Company had broken its franchise as far back as 1908, by installing a system which at that time was already considered antiquated.

2. That the state of the Telephone Company's Plant and Equipment was, at the present moment, in many respects, in a most deficient condition.

At the time when the Council, at the request of the Community, began to look into the question of the Telephone service, the Telephone Company was pressing the Council to authorize an agreement with an American Syndicate, which appeared to be disadvantageous, both from the point of view of shareholders and subscribers. As there were other parties interested in acquiring the business of the Telephone Company, I urged upon the Council the desirability of insisting upon open competition, with the result that today there are three offers in the field, all of which are far more favorable than the one which the Telephone Company wished to accept last July. Under pressure from the Council the Company has submitted these offers to an independent committee for consideration. My policy with regard to the Telephone problem would therefore appear to have been fully justified.

When I came into office, the general attitude of the Chinese members of the Community towards the Council was one of suspicion and uncertainty, and Shanghai appeared to be drifting, with the grave pos-

上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事侦缉处登记室
编号 I. O. D. 1043
日期..7.....3 - 30

卸任董事会主席在声明中
阐述辞职原因

H. E. 安诺德（Arnhold）致《字林西报》的信
概述其任期内进行的改革和工作

今年出乎意料的工部局职位选举引发的风暴暂时平息，未有进一步进展。即将离任的董事会主席空缺由副主席E. B. 麦克纳格顿准将（Brig.-General E. B. Macnaghten）填补，他将担任此职直至4月16日举行的年度纳税人大会之后。

关于上周三晚上召开的特别董事会会议上的辞职事宜，H. E. 安诺德先生向我们发送了以下信函以供发表：

《字林西报》编辑

先生：—能否借贵报版面，感谢在本次选举中支持我的本社区715名选民，他们的票数占已记录票数的一半以上，并解释我在任期届满前辞去董事会主席职务的原因？

鉴于今早贵报同行的一篇社论，以及其中提到日本选民的控制权对最终结果的影响，我觉得我有责任提请纳税人注意某些事实，了解这些事实符合他们的利益。

作为董事会主席，我无法同意强加于我的某些要求，即看似不成比例地增加日本警察以及其他事项，这些要求无法全部满足。因此，我在选举前几天得知，我将只能获得600张日本选票中的200张。如果情况确实如此，那么外侨社区必须以515票支持了我。

据了解，日本选民的投票率为90%，而英国选民约为50%。因此，显而易见，只要英国社区不更多地出来投票，工部局事务将由日本投票机器控制。也许，随着“新鲜血液”注入董事会以“整顿局面”，社区现在会对工部局事务表现出更多兴趣。

在此，请允许我提醒您，两年前我当选董事会成员时，媒体也曾表达过类似的希望？我被请求参选的主要目的是确保经济委员会的建议得到执行。在我担任主席的一年任期内，在这方面取得了以下成就：—

1. 市立医院和护理系统已重组，从而提高了效率和节约了成本。

2. 警务处处长已辞职，并从印度聘请了一位高度合格的警务行政人员来重组警力，重组工作现已接近完成。

3. 已制定方案，改善外籍和华人警队的住房及生活条件。

4. 汉文处已在新的能干负责人领导下彻底重组，旧有的被证实为浪费的制度已被废除。

5. 已启动职员重组，旨在剔除冗员，以便更多地鼓励更有前途的初级职员，提高效率，同时实现节约；这次重组的结果可能在短时间内不为公众所见。

6. 已逐步采取措施，为在工部局服务中更多地雇用能干的华人铺平道路。

7. 已任命薪俸委员会，目前正在开会研究一般薪俸问题并向董事会提出建议。

8. 已成立职员协会，旨在协调董事会与职员之间的关系。

9. 董事会整个教育体系正在重组过程中，以确保工部局的教育设施在外侨和华人社区之间平等分配，从而消除租界华人居民的一大不满根源。这次重组在实现相当大程度的节约并指引董事会教育政策方向的同时，不仅会实现节约，还将提高学校的效率，目前学校正置于一个永久性的教育委员会及学校督学的管理之下。

要完成所有这些工作还有很多事情要做，但我可以让公众来决定，我所获得的授权是否得到了坚持执行。

电话问题

去年七月，收到来自各商会和纳税人关于电话服务的紧急投诉，指出电话公司违反了其特许经营条款。

我强烈认为，鉴于董事会在此方面的责任，董事会必须聘请独立专家提供服务。电话公司和董事会在该公司董事会中的提名人反对这一提议，理由是专家的建议不会起到任何有用作用，因为公司已承诺维持现有系统。B. O. 安森先生（Mr. B. O. Anson）的服务由邮政总局 readily 提供给董事会使用，他已提交报告，公众可从中非常清楚地判断电话系统令人不满的状况以及恢复其正常运作所需的严厉措施。报告的两个主要特点显示：

1. 电话公司早在1908年就违反了其特许经营权，安装了一个在当时已被认为过时的系统。

2. 电话公司的厂房和设备目前状况在许多方面都严重不足。

当董事会应社区要求开始调查电话服务问题时，电话公司正敦促董事会批准与美国辛迪加达成协议，该协议从股东和用户角度来看似乎都不利。由于还有其他方有兴趣收购电话公司的业务，我向董事会强调坚持公开竞争的可取性，结果是今天有三份报价在场，都比电话公司去年七月希望接受的那一份有利得多。在董事会的压力下，该公司已将这些报价提交给一个独立委员会审议。因此，我关于电话问题的政策似乎得到了充分的证明。

当我上任时，社区华人成员对董事会的总体态度是怀疑和不确定的，上海似乎处于 drifting（漂移/停滞）状态，存在着严重的灾

14 A.
THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, MARCH 8, 1930

Japanese Refutes
Statement Of
H. E. Arnhold

Ridicules That Police
Question Influenced
Japanese Votes

Refuting the statement of H. E.
Arnhold, late chairman of the
Shanghai Municipal Council, that
the main cause for his non-election
at the recent poll was that he obtained only 200 of the anticipated
600 Japanese votes, due to his inability to agree to "certain requests which have been pressed
upon me for what appeared to be
a disproportionate increase in the
Japanese police and other matters,
which could not be granted in their
entirety," a prominent Japanese
ratepayer, in the course of an interview with a local evening contemporary made a statement.
He ridicules the probability of a
Japanese ratepayer ever having
given Mr. Arnhold to understand
that 600 Japanese votes would be
cast in his favor. He asks why
the Japanese ratepayers, and which
would cast even 200 votes in favor
of Mr. Arnhold if the latter takes
the stand in respect of the Japanese interests as the late chairman
of the Council has clearly expressed himself.
Discussing the recruitment of
Japanese personnel in the Shanghai
Municipal Police during the past
year he says, "To say that such
small matters as an increase in
Japanese police personnel influenced our stand in the election is, to
my mind, ridiculous. An increase,
as far as I know, was proposed by
non-Japanese members of the
Council. Additional police were
brought from Japan in conformity
with this proposal, but I know nothing of any further proposition
for the enhancement of the Japanese police personnel or the increase
of Japanese influence locally."

《字林西报》，1930年3月8日，星期六

日本人驳斥
H. E. 安诺德之声明

讥讽所谓警方问题
影响日本人选票之说

针对上海公共租界工部局前总董 H. E. 安诺德（H. E. Arnhold）的声明——其称在最近的投票中未能当选的主要原因，是他仅获得了预期600张日本选票中的200张，这是因为他无法同意“强加于我的某些要求，这些要求看似要不成比例地增加日本警察及其他事项，且无法全部予以满足”——一位知名日本纳税人在于本地一家晚报接受采访时发表了声明。

他讥讽了这样一种可能性，即曾有日本纳税人让安诺德先生以为会有600张日本选票投给他。他问道，既然工部局前总董已明确表达了他对日本利益的立场，日本纳税人为何还会，甚至会有200人投票支持安诺德先生？

在谈及过去一年上海公共租界警务处招募日本人员一事时，他说：“在我看来，说诸如增加日本警员这样的小事影响了我们在选举中的立场，是荒谬的。据我所知，增加警员是由工部局的非日本籍董事提议的。根据这一提议，从日本增派了额外警力，但我不知道有任何进一步关于增强日本警员编制或增加日本在当地影响力的提议。”

14. B.
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, MARCH 8, 1930

MR. ARNHOLD ON HIS
RESIGNING

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS."
SIR,—Though I have always ad-
mired Mr. Arnhold's eminent ability
and pre-eminent industry I confess
that I was hardly prepared for the
fine record of single-handed achieve-
ment set forth in his letter.
Obviously he thinks that in the old
Council "Eclipse was first and the
rest nowhere." This frame of
mind must make his failure at the
poll particularly disappointing,
while perhaps partly accounting for
it.
As to his references to myself,
I am sympathetic but unrepentant.
There cannot possibly be a rule
against a candidate addressing the
electors at election time.
I am, etc.,
A. D. BELL
Shanghai, March 7, 1930.

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS."
SIR,—From your admirable lead-
er of yesterday's issue referring to
Mr. Arnhold's reverse in the recent
Municipal election, any man in the
street now knows that his failure to
secure votes was mainly if not
solely due to lack of Japanese sup-
port.
The non-support of the Japanese
was due, so I infer from your leader,
to a misunderstanding derived from
an unfounded—possibly malicious—
report to the effect that Mr. Arn-
hold's firm was interested in the
Telephone Company tenders but Mr.
Arnhold has now put the issue still
clearer, though your point seems
also correct, to the effect that, as
Chairman of the Council, he had
been unable to agree to a certain
request which appeared to a dispro-
portionate increase in the Japanese
police etc. His unfortunate defeat,
therefore, was not discreditable to
him. Praise is due to you, Sir, as
well as Mr. Arnhold for having
made this clear to your readers and
since this has been made known to
the public in general, one certainly
regrets Mr. Arnhold's hard luck
owing to the, one may term, unfair
treatment, by a certain clique.
Nevertheless, Mr. Arnhold ought to
be very proud that his 716 votes,
just 20 less than the last candidate
to be elected, came, one may safely
assume, from foreign ratepayers
alone in spite of the fact that a
certain foreign quarter appeared to
have done everything possible to
check him. He would have come
out from the election triumphantly
with a record number of votes if the
Japanese had not misunderstood the
situation. However, Mr. Arnhold's
record remains that "he was a dili-
gent worker who gave freely of his
time to public affairs" and since he
gave full vent to-day in his letter
of his record during the tenure of
his office as Chairman of the Coun-
cil, he deserves the hearty thanks
of the community for all the ser-
vices he rendered.
In conclusion I would say that
your kind readers need not think the
writer a friend of Mr. Arnhold, un-
fortunately he is not.
I am, etc.,
R.
Shanghai, Mar. 7, 1930.
***We have received other letters
in answer to Mr. Arnhold's but fur-
ther than the above two go, we can
see no advantage to anyone in
publishing them. Our apologies to
the writers accordingly.—Ed.

14. B.
《字林西报》，1930年3月8日，星期六

安诺德先生谈其辞职

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生，——尽管我一直钦佩安诺德先生杰出的才能和卓越的勤勉，但我承认，对于他在信中所陈述的那份单枪匹马取得的辉煌业绩记录，我并未做好充分准备。

显然，他认为在旧的工部局中，“他是首屈一指的，其他人则不值一提”。这种心态必然使他在投票中的失利显得尤为令人失望，而这或许也在部分程度上解释了失利的原因。

至于他提及我本人之处，我表示同情但无悔意。不可能存在禁止候选人在选举期间向选民发表讲话的规定。

此致，
A. D. 贝尔（A. D. BELL）
上海，1930年3月7日

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生，——从贵报昨日社论中对安诺德先生在最近工部局选举中失利的精彩评论来看，现在街头巷尾的人都知道，他未能获得选票主要（即便不是 solely）是由于缺乏日本人的支持。

据我从贵报社论推断，日本人的不支持源于一种误解，该误解来自于一则毫无根据——可能是恶意的——报道，称安诺德先生的公司与电话公司投标事宜有利益关联。但安诺德先生现在已将问题阐述得更为清晰，尽管贵报的观点似乎也是正确的，即作为工部局总董，他无法同意某项看似要不成比例地增加日本警察等内容的要求。因此，他的不幸落败并非他的耻辱。先生，应当赞扬您以及安诺德先生向读者澄清了这一点；既然此事已为公众所知，人们确实对安诺德先生因遭受某个小团体所谓的不公平待遇而遭遇厄运感到遗憾。

尽管如此，安诺德先生理应感到非常自豪，因为他的716票（仅比最后一位当选者少20票），可以稳妥地假设，完全来自外国纳税人，尽管某些外国界别似乎已竭尽全力阻挠他。如果日本人没有误解局势，他本会以创纪录的票数 triumphantly 赢得选举。然而，安诺德先生的记录依然表明，“他是一位勤奋的工作者，慷慨地将时间奉献给公共事务”，既然他在信中充分宣泄了担任工部局总董期间的业绩记录，他理应得到社区对他所提供的所有服务的衷心感谢。

最后我要说，请贵报仁慈的读者不要认为作者是安诺德先生的朋友，不幸的是，他并不是。

此致，
R.
上海，1930年3月7日

***我们收到了其他回复安诺德先生来信的信件，但除了上述两封之外，我们认为刊登它们对任何人都没有好处。特此向作者致歉。——编者

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 8, 1936

PROVISIONAL COURT
AGREEMENT

Chinese Ratepayers Assn. and
Street Unions Protest
to Nanking

PUBLICATION OF TEXT
DEMANDED

Agitation is going on in local
Chinese circles against the new
agreement regarding the reorgan-
ization of the Shanghai Provisional
Court. On Thursday, the Chinese
Ratepayers Association and the
Amalgamated Street Unions sent
telegrams to the National Govern-
ment, expressing opposition to cer-
tain supposed provisions of the new
agreement and demanding publica-
tion of the full text without delay
so as to clear away misunderstand-
ings.

The Chinese Ratepayers Associa-
tion, in their wire, say:—
“According to the ‘Shanghai
Evening Post,’ the new agreement
recently concluded at the Provision-
al Court Reorganization Conference
stipulates that all cases involving
people who have violated the
Municipal By-laws will be dealt with
by the various Police Stations unless
the fine involved is $50 or more,
when such persons will be sent to
the reorganized Provisional Court
for trial.
“The public are amazed over this
statement and question its veracity.
The purpose of reorganizing the
Provisional Court was to bring
about the unification of China’s
judicial system and to make pre-
parations for the abolition of joint
hearing system and executive rights
of Consular Deputies in the Court.
“Whether the joint hearing system
is to be abolished in the Court is
not known to us because the new
agreement has not yet been publish-
ed. But attention should be drawn
to the fact that people who violated
the police regulations of the Inter-
national Settlement of Shanghai in
the past have been tried by the
Provisional Court even though the
fine involved only $1.
“If the ‘Evening Post’ report is
correct, then the power of the
Shanghai Municipal Police, instead
of being limited, will be greatly in-
creased because the police, being
vested with the right of imposing
fines, will arrest, detain and fine
residents at their own discretion.
This is a violation of world-
recognized judicial independence and
an encroachment upon the people’s
legal privileges. The Association
must, therefore, request you to re-
consider this question and to rectify
the errors because the residents of
Shanghai are greatly surprised by
the report appearing in the ‘Shang-
hai Evening Post’.”

Council and Agreement
Interviewed yesterday on the sub-
ject of the Provisional Court Agree-
ment, Mr. H. E. Arnhold, Chair-
man of the Shanghai Municipal
Council, stated that the agreement
had not been the subject of any
Council meeting. He himself and
Mr. Fessenden, Director of the
International Settlement, had been
consulted, which he said amounted to
the same thing as the Council taking
part in the negotiations.
Asked whether the terms obtain-
ed might have been worse, he re-
plied in the affirmative. Asked
whether they might have been
better, he answered “Of course: any-
thing can be better than it is. A
compromise of any sort is bound to
be unsatisfactory to both parties.”

《字林西报》，1936年2月8日，星期六

临时法院
协定

华人纳税会及
各马路联合会
向南京抗议

要求公布文本

当地华人圈子正针对有关重组上海临时法院的新协定进行活动。周四，华人纳税会和各马路联合总会向国民政府发出电报，表示反对新协定中某些 purported 条款，并要求立即公布全文以消除误解。

华人纳税会在电文中称：—

“据《上海晚邮报》报道，最近在临时法院重组会议上达成的新协定规定，所有涉及违反市政附例人员的案件将由各巡捕房处理，除非罚款金额在50美元或以上，此类人员将被送往重组后的临时法院受审。

“公众对此说法感到惊讶，并质疑其真实性。重组临时法院的目的是为了实现中国司法体系的统一，并为废除法院内的领事副官会审制度及执行权做准备。

“由于新协定尚未公布，我们不知晓法院内的会审制度是否将被废除。但应提请注意的事实是，过去违反上海公共租界警务规章的人员，即使罚款仅为1美元，也由临时法院审理。

“如果《晚邮报》的报道属实，那么上海公共租界警务处的权力不仅不会受到限制，反而会大大增加，因为警方被赋予罚款权后，将自行决定逮捕、拘留和罚款居民。这违反了世界公认的司法独立原则，并侵犯了人民的法律特权。因此，本会必须请求贵方重新考虑此问题并纠正错误，因为上海居民对《上海晚邮报》出现的报道深感震惊。”

工部局与协定

昨日就临时法院协定一事接受采访时，上海公共租界工部局总董 H. E. 安诺德先生表示，该协定并未成为任何工部局会议的主题。他表示，他本人与国际租界总监费森登先生（Mr. Fessenden）进行了磋商，他说这等同于工部局参与了谈判。

当被问及所获得的条款是否可能更糟时，他给予肯定回答。当被问及是否可能更好时，他回答：“当然：任何事情都可以比现状更好。任何形式的妥协必然令双方都不满意。”

The Shanghai Evening Post, Tuesday, February 11, 1930

Provisional Court
Agreement Text
Bared By Nanking
Vernacular Paper

2 Appeal Courts, Many
Other Changes Listed
Under Pact Recently
Concluded

According to the Min Kuo Pao,
vernacular paper published in Nan-
king, the text of the new agree-
ment concerning the reorganiza-
tion of the Shanghai Provisional
Court is as follows:

(1) The reorganization of the
Shanghai Provisional Court is to
make the tribunal a district court
conforming to the judicial system
of China.

(2) The Kiangsu Higher Court
is to be the appeal court for the
tribunal and the higher, and final
court for appeal will be the Nan-
king Supreme Court.

Prosecution And Jails.

(3) A prosecutors' office is to be
established in the tribunal for pro-
secuting criminals. The power
to arrest and detain the prisone-
rs is in the hands of the Minis-
try of Justice.

(4) Detention and judicial police
are to be established in the court
to execute the decisions of the tri-
bunal.

(5) The registrars and judicial
police will function under the direct
supervision and supervision of
the court. The court also has the
power to dismiss and appoint the
registrars and members of the
judicial police.

Examination Of Judges.

(6) All judges and prosecutors
are to be Chinese citizens, and
must have passed the examina-
tion for judges and prosecutors
held by the Ministry of Justice.

(7) The chief judge and the pros-
ecutor are to be appointed by the
National Government upon the
recommendation of the Ministry
of Justice. Other judges and pros-
ecutors are to be appointed by
the Ministry of Justice.

(8) The salaries of the judges
and prosecutors are to be fixed
by the Ministry of Justice.

(9) The court is to have a seal
which is to be used on all official
documents.

Further Provisions For
(1) Foreign lawyers will be
admitted to practice in the court
provided they have obtained certi-
ficates from the Ministry
of Justice which are to
be issued according to the Chinese
laws governing legal practitioners.
They are to apply Chinese law only.

(2) The police shall produce the
prisoners who are desired by the
court to be summoned or arrested
without delay. Other authorities
other than the police should obtain
special permission from the Court
before arresting and handing over
prisoners.

(10) The agreement is to be
effective for three years from the
date of signature by both parties.
This agreement may be amended
by mutual consent during the three
years, and may continue to be
effective after expiration on agree-
ment of both parties.

There also are three addenda to
the Provisional Court agreement.

Release of the text of the recent-
ly negotiated Provisional Court
Agreement has been delayed as the
representatives of the powers who
conducted the negotiations with of-
ficials of the Nanking Government,
have not received as yet acceptance
of the terms from the legations in
Peking. Release of the agreement
followed some weeks ago when
negotiations had been held up.

南京白话报纸
披露临时法院
协定文本

最近达成的协定下
列出2个上诉法院
及许多其他变更

据南京出版的白话报纸《民国报》称，关于重组上海临时法院的新协定文本如下：

(1) 上海临时法院的重组旨在使该法庭成为符合中国司法体系的地方法院。

(2) 江苏高等法院为该法庭的上诉法院，最高及终审上诉法院为南京最高法院。

检察与监狱。

(3) 法庭内将设立检察官办公室以起诉罪犯。逮捕和拘留囚犯的权力掌握在司法部手中。

(4) 法院内将设立拘留所和司法警察，以执行法庭的裁决。

(5) 书记员和司法警察将在法院的直接监督和管理下运作。法院还拥有罢免和任命书记员及司法警察成员的权力。

法官考试。

(6) 所有法官和检察官均为中国公民，且必须通过由司法部举行的法官和检察官考试。

(7) 首席法官和检察官由国民政府根据司法部的推荐任命。其他法官和检察官由司法部任命。

(8) 法官和检察官的薪金由司法部确定。

(9) 法院将拥有一枚印章，用于所有官方文件。

进一步规定
(1) 外国律师若获得司法部颁发的证书，获准在法院执业，该证书将根据管辖法律从业者的中国法律颁发。他们仅适用中国法律。

(2) 警方应立即交出法院要求传唤或逮捕的囚犯。除警方外的其他当局在逮捕和移交囚犯前，应获得法院的特别许可。

(10) 本协定自双方签字之日起生效，有效期为三年。在这三年内，经双方同意可对本协定进行修改，并在期满后经双方同意可继续有效。

临时法院协定还有三项附录。

最近谈判达成的临时法院协定文本的发布一直推迟，因为与南京政府官员进行谈判的列强代表尚未收到北京各公使馆对条款的接受。此前谈判曾陷入停滞，数周后协定的发布才得以跟进。

CHOICE OF JUDGES
Rights of Foreign Lawyers
to Practise
Nanking, Jan. 18.
It is learned that in order to ensure the efficient administration of justice by the new tribunal the candidates for the Presidency and Judgeships of the Court will be subject to careful investigation by the Judicial Officials' Selection and Examination Committee of the Ministry of Judicial Administration before being recommended to the Government for appointment.
The actual reorganization of the Court, it is stated, will be affected at the latest by April 1 next.
In regard to the question of foreign lawyers practising in the new Court, it is reliably learned that rules governing their appearance and conduct in the new Court have already been drawn up by the Ministry of Judicial Administration. All foreign lawyers must first obtain certificates from the Ministry and, according to the rules, may appear only in the reorganized Court and its immediate appellate division, the 2nd Branch Provincial High Court of Kiangsu, and also only in the following cases:
1.—Where foreign litigants are involved;
2.—Where the Shanghai Municipal Council is a complainant in a civil or criminal action and
3.—Where the Shanghai Municipal Police is the prosecutor.—Kuo Min.

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 20, 1930

CHINESE COURTS IN
SHANGHAI

The publication of the actual terms of the agreement which sets up three Chinese courts in the International Settlement in place of the old Provisional Court reveals no great novelty for those who have been following events. It only confirms their forebodings, born of the various anticipations of the agreement which have been published in the past week or two. Frankly, it must be said that the agreement conveys the impression of having been concluded, on the foreign side, by men who had no first-hand knowledge of the Provisional Court and took no advice from those who had. And this in fact appears to have been the case. The Council were never given an opportunity to consider the draft. We know this from a recent statement by the Chairman, Mr. H. E. Arnhold, who added that he himself and Mr. Fessenden, the Director General, had been consulted, "which amounted to the same thing as the Council taking part in the negotiations." With all courtesy we must emphatically point out that it is not the same thing. We feel constrained to recall that Mr. Fessenden, though undoubtedly a valuable servant of the community, is still its servant and not a Municipal Councillor; and while we have great respect for Mr. Arnhold's ability, in a matter so serious as that of the fate of the Provisional Court his opinion cannot be admitted as representing more than his personal views. We regret to have to speak thus plainly. But the Councillors generally owe it to the ratepayers to see that what has occurred in this instance does not become a precedent. The diplomatists concerned in the signing of the new agreement were enabled to report, and have no doubt reported, to their respective Governments that the Council have acquiesced in the scheme, and it is necessary to point out that the Council as such never saw it before its publication to the world. As for the Deputies, there is, what we can only call, a most unjust tendency in some quarters to imply that they were principally responsible for the troubles in the Provisional Court. That indignation may have occasionally carried them beyond the bounds of policy, is conceivable. But those who know what their experiences were prefer to think of the Deputies as conscientious men, with a clear duty to perform, who could not keep silence before the abuses they saw. Of which indeed there was no lack.

Under the new scheme there will be no Deputies, and one may faintly wonder whether their official superiors will, in the upshot, have any the easier time for being relieved of their protest. Chinese judges will sit alone and it will only be possible in certain cases for the Council to be represented by a lawyer "who may submit to the Court his views in writing during the proceedings and who may, if he deems necessary, file a petition in intervention in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure." The normal result of such representations can but too easily be imagined. One cannot but contrast the method followed in respect of the French Mixed Court, wherein the authorities of the Concession, plainly stating that they are the people responsible for the peace and order of the Concession, reserve the right to put an Assessor on the Bench when they think necessary. And for the changes actually vouchsafed, the Chinese officials have publicly expressed their pleasure and thanks. There is no apparent reason why the foreign Ministers in whose hands lay the fate of the Provisional Court should not have followed the same course in these turbulent and uncertain times. Lest it should be thought that we take too gloomy a view, let us add that we do not doubt the good faith of Dr. C. T. Wang with whom the agreement was concluded or of the President of the Judicial Yuan, under whose department the new Courts will come. Dr. Wang Chung-hui's reputation stands deservedly high and we are sure that he is as keen as anyone can be that the new Courts should be a success. But it is impossible to be blind to the fact that the Chinese Ministers with whom agreements are made are not the men with whom the ultimate power rests. The whole system of government exposes their rules to revision by some indeterminate authority in the background and opens the door to intrigue and obstruction. And what would be the Settlement's position if Nanking's enemies or local wave of Communism, say, succeeded in overthrowing them? We hope that will not happen, but it is a contingency which ought not to be overlooked by those who are supposed to care for foreign, and Chinese, interests in Shanghai.

There is proverbially no use in crying over spilt milk. It may have dwelt upon the manifold weakness of the new agreement and particularly on the not easily defensible methods by which it was reached, it is in order that we may show up in stronger relief the solitary safeguard it offers for the Council as the body responsible for the peace of Shanghai, and the vital importance of ensuring that that safeguard shall be made operative to the fullest possible extent. Article VI provides that the Council shall supply the men who are to form the judicial police of the Courts; and it is further agreed that the Council shall designate an officer "to whom will be allotted by the President an office on the Court premises and who will make an entry of all judicial processes of the Courts, such as summonses, warrants, orders and judgments, for the purpose of service or execution". No time should be lost by the Council in deciding what it can and will do under these provisions and in making known its intentions with no uncertain voice. Let us recall what happened at the beginning of 1927, when the old Mixed Court gave place to the Provisional. No preparations had been made on the foreign side; no foreigner connected with the Court from the Deputies downwards knew what his place was: the result was all sorts of pretensions on the Chinese side, a general confusion which might have degenerated into something much worse. With far greater changes in prospect on April 1, the Council must be prepared and they cannot begin their preparation too soon. This is not a departmental matter, but a vital question for the whole Council with the assistance of all the advice of those on whom will lie the duty of carrying out their decisions, and it is not to be ignored that the Council will have to make up their mind to speak plainly, to leave no doubt that they will act firmly, and that they will not be content with mere diplomatic assurances. They are the Government of Shanghai, with whom rests the supreme duty of keeping law and order in the Settlement and they can count on the unanimous support of ratepayers in making it perfectly clear that they will fulfil that duty no matter at what cost. We sincerely hope and would fain believe that the new agreement will work smoothly. But the times are too critical to allow any misplaced delicacy or waste of time in taking such precautions against mishap as that Agreement permits.

《字林西报》，1930年2月20日，星期四

上海之中国法院

确立以三所中国法院取代旧临时法院之协议条款正式公布，对于一直关注事态发展的人士而言，并未显露太多新意。这仅仅证实了他们基于过去一两周所公布之各种协议预期而产生的担忧。坦率地说，必须指出，该协议给人的印象是，外方由一些对临时法院缺乏 firsthand（第一手）了解、且未咨询知情人士的人士达成。而事实似乎确实如此。工部局从未获得审议草案之机会。我们从主席 H. E. Arnhold（安诺德）先生近期之声明中得知此事，他补充说，他自己与总办 Fessenden（费森登）先生曾受咨询，“这与工部局参与谈判无异”。出于礼貌，我们必须 emphatically（强调）指出，这并非一回事。我们感到有必要重申，Fessenden 先生虽无疑是社区之得力仆役，但其身份仍是仆役而非工部局董事；尽管我们高度尊重 Arnhold 先生之才干，但在关乎临时法院命运如此严肃之问题上，其观点不能被视为代表超出其个人意见之外之内容。我们遗憾不得不如此直言不讳。但各位董事总体上对纳税人负有责任，须确保此次发生之情况不致成为先例。签署新协议之相关外交官得以向其各自政府报告，且无疑已报告称工部局已默许该方案，因此有必要指出，工部局作为一个机构，在向世界公布之前从未见过该协议。至于副领事（Deputies），在某些方面存在一种我们只能称之为极不公正的倾向，暗示他们对临时法院之混乱负主要责任。愤慨情绪偶尔可能使他们超出策略之界限，这是可以想见的。但了解其经历之人更倾向于将副领事们视为恪尽职守、面对所见弊端无法保持沉默之人。而此类弊端确实不乏其例。

根据新方案，将不再设副领事，人们不禁轻微质疑，其上级官员在摆脱其抗议后，最终日子是否会真的更轻松。中国法官将单独坐堂，仅在特定情况下，工部局方可由一名律师代表，“该律师可在诉讼期间向法院提交书面意见，并可在认为必要时，依照《民事诉讼法》之规定提起介入诉讼”。此类陈述之通常结果不难想象。人们不禁将其与法国会审公廨所遵循之方法进行对比，在该方法中，租界当局明确声明其为负责租界和平与秩序之人，并保留在认为必要时指派陪审员（Assessor）出庭之权利。而对于实际获准之变更，中国官员已公开表示满意与感谢。在这些动荡不定之时期，掌握临时法院命运之各国驻华公使显然没有理由不采取同样之做法。以免被认为我们观点过于悲观，我们要补充说，我们毫不怀疑与之达成协议之王正廷博士之诚意，也不怀疑新法院所属之司法院院长之诚意。王宠惠博士之声望素著，我们相信他比任何人都更热切希望新法院取得成功。但不可否认之事实是，与之达成协议之中国部长们并非掌握最终权力之人。整个政府体制使其规则易受幕后某种不确定权威之修订，并为阴谋与阻挠敞开大门。倘若南京之敌人或局部共产主义浪潮成功推翻他们，租界将处于何种境地？我们希望这种情况不会发生，但这是一种不应被那些 purportedly（声称）关心上海中外利益之人所忽视之偶然情况。

谚语云，覆水难收。我们或许已详述新协议之诸多弱点，特别是其达成方式之难以辩护，但此举旨在更鲜明地突显其为作为上海和平责任主体之工部局所提供之唯一保障，并确保该保障在最大程度上生效之至关重要性。第六条规定，工部局应提供组成法院司法警察之人员；并进一步约定，工部局应指定一名官员，“由院长在法院驻地为其分配办公室，该官员负责登记所有需送达或执行之法院司法文书，如传票、逮捕令、命令及判决书”。工部局不应延误决定在此等规定下能做什么、将做什么，并以明确无误之声调公布其意图。让我们回顾1927年初发生之情况，当时旧会审公廨让位于临时法院。外方未做任何准备；从副领事以下，任何与法院有关之外籍人士均不知其职责所在：结果导致中方提出各种非分要求，造成普遍混乱，险些恶化为更糟糕之局面。鉴于4月1日将面临更大之变革，工部局必须做好准备，且越早开始准备越好。这并非部门事务，而是关乎整个工部局之 vital（重大）问题，需借助所有负责执行其决策之人之建议，且不可忽视的是，工部局必须下定决心直言不讳，不留疑余地地表明其将采取坚定行动，且不满足于 mere（仅仅）外交 assurances（保证）。他们是上海之政府，肩负着维持租界法律与秩序之 supreme（最高）职责，他们可以指望纳税人在此问题上给予一致支持，以明确表明他们将不惜任何代价履行该职责。我们真诚希望并愿意相信新协议将顺利运作。但时局过于危急，不容许因 misplaced（不当）之顾忌或浪费时间，而不采取该协议允许之预防措施以防不幸。

政治处
（外侨股）
日期 2-20

THE NORTH-CHINA · DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 22, 1930
（印：牛）

PROVISIONAL COURT
AGREEMENT
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS."
SIR,—This Agreement would ap-
pear to have been concluded so far
as the Foreign Delegates are con-
cerned by persons having no per-
sonal acquaintance during recent
years with the Court itself.
May one ask why none of the
following were consulted—
(1) The Deputies
(2) The Municipal Council
(3) The China Association
(4) The various local Cham-
bers of Commerce?
The local merchants have a great
deal at stake in connection with the
constitution of the Provisional
Court and the proper administra-
tion of justice.
In particular one would like to
know who was responsible for shut-
ting the Deputies out of the nego-
tiations whose experience would have
been invaluable to the delegates.
In short the Agreement amounts
to a virtual surrender of control to
the Chinese authorities to the de-
triment of residents of Shanghai
both foreign and Chinese.
Surely it would have been better
to await Judge Natham's re-
port and the conclusion of the
extraterritoriality negotiation be-
fore concluding a new agree-
ment for a period of three
years bearing in mind that the fu-
ture status of Shanghai is so much
bound up with the welfare of the
Provisional Court.
I am, etc.,

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS MONDAY, FEBRUARY 24, 1930

THE SURRENDER OF
CHINESE

Reference was made in a Note
and Comment on Saturday to the
clause in Article VI of the new
Chinese Courts agreement for
Shanghai under which it will be
possible for demands to be made
from outside the Settlement for
the surrender of any Chinese
living in it, and on proof of
identity the Court in Shanghai
will simply hand the man over
forthwith. This clause is so
extremely serious, so fraught
with danger for all Chinese busi-
ness men living in Shanghai,
that even at this late hour, when
this bad agreement has actually
been signed, every possible effort
should be made to introduce
some safeguard, or at least to
have the operation of the clause
more clearly defined. For gen-
eral convenience we repeat it:
"No person found in the Interna-
tional Settlement shall be handed
to the extra-Settlement autho-
rities without a preliminary in-
vestigation in court at which
counsel for the accused shall have
the right to be present and heard,
except in the case of requests
emanating from other Modern Law
Courts when the accused may be
handed over after his identity has
been established by the Court.
If the demand for the surrender
of any person comes from a
"Modern Law Court," it would
seem that no specific charge
need be laid, no counsel can be
present, the accused can say
nothing in his own defence: if
the local Court is satisfied that
he is the man wanted, it must
hand him over. In the first
place, what is to be the definition
of a "Modern Law Court"? So
far as can be seen, anything
might be called that, and pro-
bably would be if the "wanted"
man were wanted badly enough.
Furthermore, how will the "Mo-
dern Law Court" arrive at the
conclusions on which it will de-
mand the surrender of an in-
dividual? In the new Courts in
Shanghai the procurator will
have to work in public, that
is one of the small safeguards
secured by the new agreement.
But in other Chinese Courts the
procurator's proceedings take
place in camera and there
appears no reason to suppose
that this practice will be
changed whether in modern or
ancient courts. The accused
man will know nothing of the
crime alleged against him until,
having been seized by the Judi-
cial police of the Shanghai Court,
he is bundled across the border
into the hands of those who are

During the course of the Pro-
visional Court conference it was
stated as a principle on the
foreigners' side that they are
not concerned to defend Chinese
against their own officials. A
more utterly pernicious half-
truth it would be difficult to
imagine, nor one which betray-
ed more hopeless ignorance of
abuses that always have been
practised in China and are pos-
sibly more flagrant to-day than
they have ever been. In the
sense that residence in the In-
ternational Settlement does not
confer extraterritorial status on
Chinese, and that the Council
would never dream of trying to
prevent a man against whom
there was a bona fide charge
from being handed over to the
extra-Settlement authorities,
this statement is true enough.
But as the party responsible for
the peace and good order of the
Settlement the Council are in
duty bound to satisfy themselves
that there is a genuine presump-
tion of guilt in the man whose
surrender is demanded and that
he is not merely the victim of
a private quarrel or one whose
wealth has exposed him to official
cupidity. We have but last
week seen what is likely to hap-
pen, in the case of the two
indigo merchants whose surren-
der, on a palpably flimsy charge,
was demanded by the District
Court of Shanghai, and who had
already fled to Tientsin although
the Rendition agreement, which
is still operative, should have
given them protection. It is
not too much to say that Article
VI of the new agreement will
spread terror among Chinese
merchants in the Settlement and
is a serious danger to the
prosperity of Shanghai.
This article intensifies the
need to which we referred last
Thursday of the Council losing
no time in making up their minds
as to what they can do and, even
more importantly, what they will
not consent to do, under the new
agreement. The fact that the
Council will apply the men from
whom the judicial police are to
be appointed gives them an op-
portunity to get safeguards in-
troduced into the operation of
Clause VI. It would be nothing
short of a disgrace if municipal
police could be employed for
what, as the clause stands, is no
better than legalised kidnapping.
If the worst came to the worst,
it might well be necessary for
the Council to refuse to allow
the police to act as agents at all,
unless some guarantee as to
their use were forthcoming. In
this connection there should be
a clear understanding as to the
steps which the Council may
take with regard to the Court's readiness

to record all its judicial pro-
cesses,
"such as summonses, warrants,
orders and judgments for the pur-
pose of service or execution in
accordance with the provision of
the above mentioned article" (VI)
In what room is he to sit? Who
is he to be? In what language
will his records be kept? What
staff—a very important matter
—will he have? These are vital
questions, and the Council can-
not insist too early-on obtaining
full satisfaction on them.

（批：U.D.C. I.

article seems like
very important. I
agree with the
statements which are
underlined. For your
information.

《字林西报》 1930年2月24日，星期一

中国人的引渡

在周六的“笔记与评论”栏目中，曾提及上海新设中国法院协定第六条中的一项条款。根据该条款，租界以外方面可要求引渡任何居住在租界内的中国人，而在身份得到证实后，上海法院将 simply（径直）将该人移交。此条款极其严重，对居住在上海的所有中国商人充满危险，以至于即便在此坏协定已然签署的迟暮时刻，仍应尽一切努力引入某种保障，或至少使该条款的运作更加明确界定。为便于大众了解，现重申该条款原文：“凡在国际租界内发现之人，未经法院初步审讯——被告律师有权在场并陈述意见——不得移交给租界外当局；但若请求来自其他‘现代法律法院’，则在法院确认其身份后，可将被告移交。”如果引渡某人的要求来自一家“现代法律法院”，看来似乎无需提出具体指控，律师不得在场，被告也无法为自己辩护：只要地方法院确信此人即为被通缉者，就必须将其移交。首先，“现代法律法院”的定义是什么？就目前所见，任何法院都可能被称为此名，而且如果对该“被通缉”者的追捕足够迫切，很可能就会如此称呼。此外，“现代法律法院”将如何得出要求其引渡个人的结论？在上海的新式法院中，检察官必须公开行事，这是新协定所确保的微小保障之一。但在其他中国法院，检察官的诉讼程序是秘密进行的，且没有理由认为这种做法会在现代或古代法院中有所改变。被告人在被上海法院的司法警察抓获并强行带过边界、落入那些人之手前，对自己被指控的罪行将一无所知。

在临时法院会议期间，外方代表曾声明一项原则，即他们无意保护中国人免受其本国官员的处置。很难想象还有比这更有害的半真半假之辞，也没有哪种说法更能暴露出对中国历来存在的、且今日可能比以往任何时候都更为猖獗的弊政的绝望无知。就国际租界的居留权并不赋予中国人治外法权地位，且工部局绝不会试图阻止将面对真实指控的人移交给租界外当局这一意义而言，该声明确属属实。但是，作为负责租界和平与良好秩序的一方，工部局有义务确信，被要求引渡之人确实存在犯罪的合理嫌疑，而不仅仅是私人纠纷的受害者，或其财富使其成为官方贪婪目标的牺牲品。就在上周，我们看到了可能发生的情况：两名靛蓝商人在上海地方法院以明显站不住脚的罪名要求引渡他们时，虽已逃往天津，但本应给予他们保护的《交还章程》（Rendition agreement）仍在生效。可以说，新协定的第六条将在租界内的中国商人中散布恐慌，并对上海的繁荣构成严重威胁。

本文加剧了我们上周四所提及的紧迫需求，即工部局需尽快下定决心，明确在新协定下他们能做什么，以及更重要的是，他们不会同意做什么。工部局将任命司法警察的人员来源这一事实，为他们提供了在第六条款的执行中引入保障措施的机会。如果按照该条款目前的措辞，市政警察被用于无异于合法化绑架的行为，那将是莫大的耻辱。若情况恶化至极点，工部局可能有必要拒绝允许警察充当代理人，除非能就其使用方式提供某种保证。在此方面，应就工部局针对法院准备记录其所有司法程序（“如传票、逮捕令、命令和判决书，以便按照上述第VI条的规定进行送达或执行”）的步骤达成明确谅解。他将在哪个房间办公？他将由谁担任？他的记录将使用何种语言？他将拥有怎样的职员队伍——这是一个非常重要的问题——？这些都是至关重要的问题，工部局必须尽早坚持获得对此的充分满意答复。

（批注：U.D.C. I.

似乎非常重要。我
同意其中划下划线
的陈述。供你
参考。
J.H.S.

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 26, 1930

COUNCIL AND
POWERS

The implication of recent articles, as readers will readily have seen, is that the Municipal Council must assert itself and take a determined line where its duty calls and its rights are at stake. In some quarters this seems to have been taken to mean that the Council generally should defy the Powers, suggesting that Shanghai intends to manage its own business and would be glad to see them manage theirs. This is surely an irrational, exaggerated interpretation of a quite reasonable principle, the easy refuge of those who only seek the line of least resistance. Because the Powers have declared their readiness to meet China's wishes as and when it may be feasible to do so, it does not follow that they are merely competing with each other to see who can throw everything away first, and it is a bad mistake to assume that this is their resolve, and consequently that there is nothing for us in Shanghai to do but to sit with folded hands and await our doom.

Three important facts should be borne in mind in this connection. First, let us again quote from the British aide-mémoire handed to the Nanking Government at the close of last December. The concluding sentence reads as follows:

His Majesty's Government are ready to enter into detailed negotiations, as soon as political conditions in China render it possible to do so, with a view to agreeing on a method and a programme for carrying abolition of extraterritoriality into effect by gradual and progressive stages to the mutual satisfaction of both governments.

It may safely be assumed that other Powers would, on the whole, endorse this attitude; certainly they would not proceed more quickly; probably they would be even more cautious. But the passages we have italicized show conclusively that the Foreign Office does not lose sight of certain clear safeguards and stipulations which must be fulfilled before it can meet Chinese wishes in full. From Shanghai's point of view this statement is of the greatest importance. Shanghai itself is the very core of the whole question of extraterritoriality. Any measures tending towards the removal of consular jurisdiction must strike at the independence of Shanghai. If, then, a Minister is found exceeding the pace set by his own government, or interfering in negotiations which affect Shanghai as a whole without the knowledge and consent of his colleagues in Peking, the Council have every right to take exception to his conduct and to shape their own course, regardless of any attempt at dictation by him.

The second fact which may justly be stressed is that the Council are the only government of Shanghai, responsible for the maintenance of law and order and the protection of its interests, both Chinese and foreign, until the situation under which it has always functioned is reversed. Wild and gloomy statements have been repeated to us that "the Powers could wipe out Shanghai with a stroke of the pen." There is no doubt they could do so. There is equally no doubt that they would never dream of doing so. It is an old saying that "circumstances alter cases." What the Powers might possibly have felt justified in doing as regards Shanghai even fifty years ago would be at once recognized as quite inadmissible today, when Shanghai has become one of the largest and most important cities in the world. If the Council could show reasonable cause for any line of action they felt bound to take, the Powers would never repudiate them, and we may further be confident that they would not disregard the Council's wishes if these were firmly enough expressed. If the Council's representations on certain matters have, in the past, been rejected in London or Washington, that was not because they were unreasonable or inequitable, but simply because the demand was not pressed with sufficient resolution.

And the third fact to be remembered is the appointment of Judge Feetham. He has been brought here to study the history and problems of Shanghai and to advise on its future constitution conformably with the satisfaction of Chinese wishes and the protection of Chinese and foreign business interests. It has been made known unofficially that the principal Powers welcomed Judge Feetham's appointment and will be pleased to consider the scheme he may suggest for the solution of a problem which no one yet has attempted to solve. The obvious corollary of this attitude is that the Powers shall wait, before making any changes liable to affect Shanghai, until Judge Feetham has finished his work. By calling him to do that work at its own expense, the foreign community of Shanghai has given unequivocal proof that it accepts the principle that changes are in store, and is doing its utmost to assist in their execution. This fact gives it the right to ask that the scope of Judge Feetham's inquiry shall not be capriciously restricted or the ground cut from under his feet. By the fact alone of having called in such an advisor, the Council are put in an unassailably strong position to insist that, while they still remain the government of Shanghai, they shall not be hampered in the execution of their duty.

It may further be emphasized that the Council is one, a continuous, unchanged government, based on many decades of tradition, custom, precedent, and wide experience. The Diplomatic Body, for practical purposes, is too often only an expression: actually, it is composed of sixteen or seventeen men liable to pull in as many different directions, always subject to orders from political parties thousands of miles away whose views are perpetually influenced by the wish to catch and retain votes at home; and these men, sent out here for a few years to represent their respective governments, would be more than human if their principal preoccupation were not to avoid doing anything which might endanger their chances of a better post when they are moved on from China. In all complicated questions the man who makes up his mind to a given line of action and follows it without fear or favour is the one most sure of success. It is a maxim which the Council may be urged to keep clearly before their eyes. The fear that the Powers would throw us down or repudiate us is, frankly, rubbish. The Council have not been given to acting without reason and reflection in the past, and they are not likely to do so at any time. More than once in recent years we have heard from London that it was impossible for the British Government to understand what Shanghai really wanted, so many and different were the opinions uttered by Shanghai men. That is the Council's opportunity, to take the lead conformably with the facts set out above and to keep it resolutely.

（批：拟 陈）

《字林西报》，1930年2月26日，星期三

工部局与
列强

读者不难看出，近期文章的言外之意是，工部局必须彰显自身力量，在职责所在且权利受到威胁时采取坚定立场。在某些方面，这似乎被理解为工部局整体应当违抗列强，暗示上海打算管理自己的事务，并乐见列强管好他们自己的事。这无疑是对一个相当合理原则的非理性、夸张解读，是那些只求走阻力最小路线的人的轻易避风港。列强已声明愿意在可行之时满足中国的愿望，但这并不意味着它们只是在相互竞争，看谁能最先抛弃一切；若假定这是它们的决心，进而认为我们在上海除了束手待毙之外别无他法，那是一个严重的错误。

在此问题上，有三项重要事实应铭记于心。首先，让我们再次引用去年年底递交给南京政府的英国备忘录。其结尾句如下：

英王陛下政府准备一旦中国政治局势允许，即进行详细谈判，以期就逐步分阶段废除治外法权的方法和方案达成一致，使两国政府均感满意。

可以稳妥地假定，其他列强总体上会赞同这一态度；当然，它们不会进展得更快；可能甚至会更加谨慎。但我们用斜体标出的段落确凿地表明，外交部并未忽视某些明确的保障措施和规定，这些必须在完全满足中国愿望之前得以履行。从上海的角度来看，这一声明至关重要。上海本身是整个治外法权问题的核心。任何旨在取消领事裁判权的措施都必然冲击上海的独立性。因此，如果发现某位公使超越其本国政府设定的步伐，或在未经其北京同僚知晓和同意的情况下干涉影响整个上海的谈判，工部局完全有权对其行为提出异议，并规划自身的行动路线，而不顾其任何发号施令的企图。

其次，值得强调的事实是，工部局是上海唯一的政府，负责维持法律与秩序，保护其中外利益，直至其一贯运作的局势发生逆转。有人向我们反复散布狂野而悲观的言论，称“列强只需笔尖一动便可抹去上海”。毫无疑问，它们确实能做到这一点。但同样毫无疑问的是，它们绝不会梦想这样做。俗话说，“情况变化，案例亦变”。即使是在五十年前，列强可能就上海问题认为正当的做法，在今日上海已成为世界上最大、最重要的城市之一时，会被立即认定为完全不可接受。如果工部局能为其感到必须采取的任何行动路线提供合理理由，列强绝不会予以否认；我们还可以确信，如果工部局的意愿表达得足够坚定，列强也不会置之不理。过去，工部局在某些事项上的交涉在伦敦或华盛顿遭到拒绝，并非因为这些要求不合理或不公平，而仅仅是因为提出这些要求时缺乏足够的决心。

第三项需要记住的事实是费唐法官（Judge Feetham）的任命。他被请来这里研究上海的历史和问题，并就其未来宪制提供建议，以符合满足中国愿望和保护中外商业利益的要求。非正式消息透露，主要列强欢迎费唐法官的任命，并乐意考虑他可能提出的解决这一迄今无人尝试解决的问题的方案。这种态度显而易见的推论是，在费唐法官完成工作之前，列强应等待，不进行任何可能影响上海的变更。上海的外侨社区自费聘请他从事这项工作，已明确证明其接受变革即将到来的原则，并正竭尽全力协助执行。这一事实赋予了它要求不得随意限制费唐法官调查范围或拆其台基的权利。仅凭聘请这样一位顾问这一事实，工部局便处于无可辩驳的强势地位，可以坚持认为，在其仍作为上海政府期间，其履行职责不应受到阻碍。

还可以进一步强调，工部局是一个统一的、连续的、未变的政府，建立在数十年的传统、习俗、先例和广泛经验之上。外交团在实际操作中往往只是一个名义：实际上，它由十六或十七人组成，这些人可能朝着同样多的不同方向拉扯，始终受制于数千英里外政党的命令，而这些政党的观点不断受到在国内争取和保持选票的愿望的影响；这些人被派到这里代表各自政府任职几年，如果他们的主要关切不是避免做任何可能危及他们离开中国后获得更好职位的机会的事情，那他们就超乎常人地高尚了。在所有复杂的问题中，下定决心采取既定行动路线并不畏不偏地遵循的人，是最有可能成功的人。这是一条格言，建议工部局将其清晰地置于眼前。担心列强会抛弃或否认我们，坦率地说，是无稽之谈。工部局过去从未无故且不加反思地行事，将来也不太可能这样做。近年来，我们不止一次从伦敦听到，英国政府无法理解上海真正想要什么，因为上海人士发表的意见如此之多且各不相同。这正是工部局的机会，按照上述事实采取领导地位，并坚决保持这一地位。

Note From Heads of Legations

Nanking, Feb. 17.
Sir:—With reference to the
Agreement which we have signed
to-day concerning the establish-
ment of a District Court and a
Branch High Court in the Inter-
national Settlement at Shanghai,
we have the honour to request
your confirmation of our under-
standing on the following points:

1.—It is understood that the
Courts established under the pre-
sent Agreement shall exercise
jurisdiction over civil and criminal
cases as well as police offences
and inquests in the International
Settlement at Shanghai, provided
that the jurisdiction of the said
Courts over persons shall be the
same as that of other Chinese
Courts and provided that their
territorial jurisdiction shall be
the same as that of the Chinese
Court now functioning in the
International Settlement at Shang-
hai, except (a) mixed criminal
cases arising on private foreign
property outside the limits of the
Settlement and (b) mixed civil
cases arising in areas surrounding
the Settlement.
2.—It is understood that the
present practice regarding the re-
spective jurisdictions of the Chin-
ese Court now functioning in the
International Settlement and the
Court existing in the French
Concession shall be followed,
pending a definite arrangement
between the Chinese Government
and the authorities concerned.
3.—It is understood that as far
as practicable, Chinese shall be
recommended by the Municipal
Council to serve as officers and
members of the judicial police of
the Court established under the
present Agreement. It is further
understood that among the officers
of the judicial police appointed by
the President of the Branch High
Court under Article VI of the pre-
sent Agreement, there will be one
to be designated by the Municipal
Council, to whom will be allotted
by the President an office on the
court premises and who will make
an entry of all judicial processes
of the Courts, such as summonses,
warrants, orders and judgments,
for the purpose of service or ex-
ecution in accordance with the pro-
visions of the above-mentioned
Article.
4.—It is understood that the
establishment of the Courts pro-
vided for in the present Agree-
ment in no way affects the validity
of judgments rendered by the
Court now functioning in the
International Settlement and its
predecessor, and that such judg-
ments shall be considered as final
and valid except where an appeal
has been lawfully taken or re-
served. It is further understood
that the judgments of the courts
established under the present
Agreement shall be on the same
footing as regards validity as the
judgments of all other Chinese
courts.
5.—It is understood that the
present Agreement does not in
any way affect or prejudice any
future negotiations regarding the
status of extra-Settlement roads.
6.—It is understood that the
sum of $60,000 (sixty thousand
dollars) now on deposit with the
Bank of China to the credit of the
present Chinese Court in the Inter-
national Settlement shall be main-
tained by the Chinese Government
to the credit of the new Courts
established under the present
Agreement.

7.—It is agreed that in accord-
ance with Chinese law, there shall
be maintained by the Courts
established under the present
Agreement, a storage room for
articles confiscated by the Courts,
which remain the property of the
Chinese Government, it being
understood that confiscated opium
and instruments for the smoking
and preparation thereof shall be
burned publicly in the International
Settlement every three months
and that the Municipal Council
may present to the presidents of
the Courts for transmission to the
Ministry of Justice such sugges-
tions as it may desire to make re-
garding the disposal of confiscated
arms.
8.—It is understood that upon
the coming into force of the pre-
sent Agreement, all cases pending
in the Chinese Court now func-
tioning in the International
Settlement shall be dealt with in
the Courts established under the
present Agreement in accordance
with the procedure in force in the
latter Courts, provided that the
proceedings in mixed cases shall,
as far as practicable, be continued
from the point where they are
taken over and concluded within a
period of twelve months which
period may be extended at the dis-
cretion of the Court when the cir-
cumstances in any case so war-
rant.
J. de Pinto Dias on be-

the American Minister Joseph E.
Jacobs; W. Meyrick Hewlett on
behalf of His Britannic Majesty's
Minister; L. Gronvold on behalf of

有权根据本条在上述法院执业的外国律师，应向司法部申请律师证书，并须遵守适用于律师的中国法律法规，包括有关纪律惩处的规定。

第九条

应任命四名常任代表，其中两名由中国政府任命，另两名由签署本协议的其他列强政府任命。他们应共同寻求调和关于本协议解释或适用的意见分歧，此类分歧可由分院高等法院院长或签署协议的外国列强当局提交给他们处理。但除非经双方同意，他们的报告对任何一方均无约束力。需明确的是，法院本身的任何判决、决定、裁定或命令不得提交上述代表审议。

第十条

本协议及所附照会应于1930年4月1日生效，并自该日起继续有效三年，但经各方相互同意，可延长有效期。

1930年2月17日签于南京。

有关各国驻华公使致外交部长的照会

南京，2月17日。

先生：——关于我们今日签署的关于在上海公共租界设立地方法院和高等法院分院的协议，我们荣幸地请求您确认我们对以下各点的理解：

1. 兹理解，根据本协议设立的法院将对上海公共租界内的民事和刑事案件以及违警罪案件和验尸案件行使管辖权，但上述法院对人的管辖权应与其他中国法院相同，且其地域管辖权应与目前在上海公共租界运作的中国法院相同，惟下列情况除外：(a) 发生在租界界限以外的私人外国财产上的混合刑事案件，以及 (b) 发生在租界周边地区的混合民事案件。

2. 兹理解，在中国政府与有关当局达成明确安排之前，应遵循目前关于在上海公共租界运作的中国法院与法租界内现有法院各自管辖权的现行做法。

3. 兹理解，在切实可行的范围内，工部局应推荐中国人担任根据本协议设立的法院的司法警察官员及成员。进一步理解，在根据本协议第六条由高等法院分院院长任命的司法警察官员中，将有一名由工部局指定，院长将在法院办公场所内为其分配一间办公室，该官员将根据上述条款的规定，为送达或执行之目的，记录法院的所有司法文书，如传票、逮捕令、命令和判决书。

4. 兹理解，本协议规定的法院的设立，绝不影响目前在上海公共租界运作的法院及其前身所作出的判决的有效性，此类判决应被视为终局且有效，除非已依法提起上诉或保留上诉权。进一步理解，根据本协议设立的法院的判决，在有效性方面应与所有其他中国法院的判决具有同等地位。

5. 兹理解，本协议绝不以任何方式影响或损害关于越界筑路地位的任何未来谈判。

6. 兹理解，目前存于中国银行、记入上海公共租界现设中国法院名下的60,000美元（陆万美元）款项，应由中国政府维持并存入根据本协议设立的新法院名下。

7. 兹同意，根据中国法律，根据本协议设立的法院应设立一个储藏室，用于存放被法院没收的物品，这些物品仍属中国政府所有。需明确的是，没收的鸦片及吸食和制备鸦片的器具，每三个月应在公共租界内公开焚毁；工部局可就没收武器的处置问题，向各法院院长提出其希望提出的建议，由院长转呈司法部。

8. 兹理解，在本协议生效后，目前在上海公共租界运作的中国法院中所有未结案件，均应根据新设法院现行的程序，在根据本协议设立的法院中处理。但混合案件的诉讼程序，在切实可行的范围内，应从接管时的阶段继续进行，并在十二个月内审结；若任何案件的情况有此需要，法院可自行决定延长该期限。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 19, 1930.

Text Of New Provisional
Court Agreement Issued;
Goes Into Effect April 1

Deputy System Is Abolished In Re-organized Court;
Ministries At Nanking Consider Question Of New Personnel

Following the signing at Nanking on Monday of the agreement relative to the re-organization of the Shanghai Provisional Court, a meeting of the ranking members of the Ministry of Judicial Administration including Minister Wei Tao-ming and Counsellors Wu and Chien Tai, was held under the chairmanship of President Wang Chung-hui of the Judicial Yuan to decide, upon the re-organization measures to be adopted for the Court.

It is understood that in order to carry out the efficient administration of justice by the new tribunal the candidates for the Presidency and Judgeships of the Court will be subject to careful examination by the judicial officer selection and examination committee of the Ministry of Judicial Administration before being recommended to the Government for appointment.

Actual re-organization of the Court, it is said, will be effected at the latest by April 1 of the current year.

In regard to the question of foreign lawyers practising in the new Court, it is reliably learned that they will be allowed to appear as counsel provided that they possess certificates from their respective consulates according to the rules of the bar and its immediate jurisdiction, the Branch High Court of Kiangsu being the only one in the following:

1.—When both litigants are foreigners.
2.—When the Shanghai Municipal Council is complainant in a civil or criminal action and
3.—When the Shanghai Municipal Council is prosecutor.
Kuo Ming.

The full text of the agreement follows:

From the date on which the present Agreement comes into force, all laws, regulations, judgments, and decisions having effect prior to the establishment of the Courts in the International Settlement at Shanghai shall be abolished.

Article II

The Chinese Government shall in accordance with Chinese laws and regulations relating to the judiciary and subject to the terms of the present Agreement, establish in the International Settlement at Shanghai a District Court (Ti Fang Fa Yuan) and a Branch High Court (Kao Teng Fa Yuan Fen Yuan). All Chinese laws and regulations, substantive as well as procedural, which are now in force, or which may hereafter be duly enacted and promulgated shall be applicable in the courts, due account being taken of the Land Regulations and Bye-laws of the International Settlement, which are applicable pending their adoption and promulgation by the Chinese Government, and of the terms of the present Agreement.

Judgments, decisions and rulings of the Branch High Court are subject to appeal, according to Chinese law, to the Supreme Court of China.

Article III

The former practice of consular deputies or consular officials appearing to watch proceedings, or to sit jointly in the Chinese Court now functioning in the International Settlement shall be discontinued in the Courts established under the present Agreement.

Article IV

When any person is arrested by the municipal or judicial police, he shall, within 24 hours, exclusive of holidays, be sent to the Courts established under the present Agreement to be dealt with, failing which he shall be released.

Article V

The Courts established under the present Agreement shall each have a certain number of procurators to be appointed by the Chinese Government, who shall hold inquests and autopsies (Chien Yen) within the jurisdiction of these Courts and shall otherwise perform their functions in accordance with Chinese law in all cases involving the application of Articles 103 to 120 of the Chinese Criminal Code, except where the municipal police of the International Settlement or the party concerned has already initiated prosecution, provided that all preliminary investigations conducted by the procurator shall be held publicly and counsel for the accused shall have the right to be present and heard.

In other cases arising within the jurisdiction of the courts, the municipal police or the party concerned shall prosecute. The procurator shall have the right to express his views in court in all criminal cases in which the prosecution is initiated by the Municipal Police or the party concerned.

Article VI

All judicial processes, such as summonses, warrants, orders, etc., shall be valid only after they have been signed by a judge of the Courts established under the present Agreement, whereupon they shall be served or executed by the judicial police or, as provided below, by the process-servers thereof.

No person found in the International Settlement shall be handed over to the extra-Settlement authorities without a preliminary identification in court, at which counsel for the accused shall have the right to be present and heard, except in the case of requests emanating from other modern law courts when the accused may be handed over after his identity has been established by the Court.

All judgments, decisions and rulings of the Courts shall be executed as soon as they become final as a result of the judicial procedure in force shall render any assistance within their power may be requested of them.

The process-servers of the Courts shall be appointed by the Presidents of the Courts respectively, and their duties shall be to serve all summonses and deliver other documents of the Courts in connection with civil cases. For the execution of judgments in civil cases, the process-servers shall be accompanied by the judicial police. The officers and members of the judicial police of the Courts shall be appointed by the President of the Branch High Court upon the recommendation of the Municipal Council and shall be subject to dismissal by the President of that Court upon cause shown. Their services will also be terminated by the President at the request of the Municipal Council, upon cause shown. They shall wear the uniform designed by the Chinese judicial authorities, and shall be subject to the orders and direction of the Courts and faithful to their duties.

Article VII

The House of Detention for civil cases and the Women's Prison attached to the Chinese court now functioning in the International Settlement at Shanghai shall be transferred from that Court to the Courts established under the present Agreement and shall be supervised and administered by the Chinese authorities.

All prisoners now serving sentences in the prisons attached to the Chinese Court now functioning in the International Settlement and those sentenced by the Courts established under the present Agreement shall, at the discretion of the said Courts, serve their sentences either in such prisons in the Settlement or in Chinese prisons outside the Settlement, except that offenders against the Police Offences Code and the Land Regulations and Bye-Laws and persons under arrest awaiting trial shall serve their periods of detention in the Settlement. The prisons in the Settlement shall be operated, as far as practicable, in conformity with Chinese prison regulations and shall be subject to inspection, from time to time, by officers appointed by the Chinese judicial authorities.

Persons sentenced to death by the Courts established under the present Agreement shall be sent to the Chinese authorities outside of the Settlement for execution of such sentence.

Article VIII

Foreign lawyers duly qualified will be admitted to practice in the Courts established under the present Agreement in all cases in which a foreigner is a party,

据悉，为确保新法庭高效施行司法，法院院长及法官候选人须经司法行政部司法人员甄选考试委员会严格审查，方可推荐政府任命。

据称，法院的实际改组工作最迟将于本年4月1日前完成。

关于外国律师在新法院执业的问题，据可靠消息，只要其按照律师公会及其直接管辖机构的规定持有各自领事馆颁发的证书，即获准出庭辩护。江苏高等法院分院是唯一拥有以下管辖权的法院：

1. 诉讼双方均为外国人时。
2. 上海工部局在民事或刑事诉讼中为原告时，以及
3. 上海工部局为公诉人时。
郭明（音译）。

协定全文如下：

自本协定生效之日起，此前在上海公共租界法院设立之前生效的所有法律、法规、判决和裁定均予废止。

第二条

中国政府应依照中国有关司法的法律和法规，并根据本协定的条款，在上海公共租界设立地方法院（Ti Fang Fa Yuan）和高等法院分院（Kao Teng Fa Yuan Fen Yuan）。所有现行有效或今后经正式制定和颁布的中国实体法及程序法法律和法规，均适用于上述法院，但应适当考虑在由中国政府采纳和颁布之前适用的《土地章程》及附则，以及本协定的条款。

高等法院分院的判决、裁定和裁决，依中国法律可向中华民国最高法院上诉。

第三条

以前由领事副手或领事官员出庭观审，或在目前于公共租界内运作的中国法院中会同坐堂的做法，在根据本协定设立的法院中应予停止。

第四条

任何人被市政警察或司法警察逮捕后，应在24小时内（节假日除外）送交根据本协定设立的法院处理，否则应予释放。

第五条

根据本协定设立的各法院应设有若干名由中国政府任命的检察官，他们应在这些法院的管辖范围内进行验尸和尸检（Chien Yen），并在涉及适用《中华民国刑法》第103条至第120条的所有案件中，依照中国法律履行其职能，但公共租界市政警察或有关当事人已提起公诉的情况除外；前提是检察官进行的所有初步调查均应公开举行，被告辩护人有权在场并发表意见。

在法院管辖范围内发生的其他案件中，应由市政警察或有关当事人提起公诉。在所有由市政警察或有关当事人提起公诉的刑事案件中，检察官有权在法庭上发表意见。

第六条

所有司法文书，如传票、逮捕令、命令等，仅在由根据本协定设立的法院的法官签署后方为有效，随后应由司法警察送达或执行，或如下文所述由其执达员送达或执行。

在公共租界内发现的任何人，未经法庭初步身份确认，不得移交给租界以外的当局，在此过程中被告辩护人有权在场并发表意见；但若请求来自其他现代法治法院，则在法院确认其身份后，可移交被告人。

法院的所有判决、裁定和裁决一经司法程序终结而生效，即应予以执行；如有需要，可在其能力范围内请求协助。

法院的执达员由各法院院长分别任命，其职责是送达所有传票并交付与民事案件有关的其他法院文件。在执行民事案件的判决时，执达员应由司法警察陪同。法院司法警察的官员和成员应由高等法院分院院长根据工部局的推荐任命，并在有正当理由的情况下由该法院院长予以免职。经工部局请求并有正当理由时，院长也可终止其服务。他们应穿着中国司法机关设计的制服，服从法院的命令和指挥，并忠于职守。

第七条

附属于目前在上海公共租界内运作的中国法院的民事拘留所和女子监狱，应从该法院移交给根据本协定设立的法院，并由中国当局监督和管理。

目前在公共租界内运作的中国法院附属监狱中服刑的所有囚犯，以及由根据本协定设立的法院判刑的囚犯，可由上述法院酌情决定，在租界内的此类监狱或租界外的中国监狱服刑；但违反《违警律》、《土地章程》及附则的罪犯，以及待审的被捕人员，应在租界内服拘留期。租界内的监狱应在可行范围内按照中国监狱规章运作，并应不时接受由中国司法机关任命的官员的检查。

由根据本协定设立的法院判处死刑的人，应送往租界外的中国当局执行该刑罚。

第八条

具备正式资格的外国律师，在凡有外国人作为当事人的案件中，获准在根据本协定设立的法院执业，

62 THE MUNICIPAL GAZETTE, FRIDAY, MARCH 7, 1930.

Agreement Relating to the Chinese Courts in the International Settlement at Shanghai.

ARTICLE I.

From the date on which the present Agreement comes into force, all former rules, agreements, exchanges of notes et cetera, having special reference to the establishment of a Chinese court in the International Settlement at Shanghai shall be abolished.

ARTICLE II.

The Chinese Government shall, in accordance with Chinese laws and regulations relating to the judiciary and subject to the terms of the present Agreement, establish in the International Settlement at Shanghai a District Court (Ti Fang Fa Yuan) and a Branch High Court (Kao Teng Fa Yuan Fen Yuan). All Chinese laws and regulations, substantive as well as procedural, which are now in force, or which may hereafter be duly enacted and promulgated shall be applicable in the Courts, due account being taken of the Land Regulations and Byelaws of the International Settlement, which are applicable pending their adoption and promulgation by the Chinese Government, and of the terms of the present Agreement.
Judgments, decisions and rulings of the Branch High Court are subject to appeal, according to Chinese law, to the Supreme Court of China.

ARTICLE III.

The former practice of Consular deputies or Consular officials appearing to watch proceedings or to sit jointly in the Chinese court now functioning in the International Settlement shall be discontinued in the Courts established under the present Agreement.

ARTICLE IV.

When any person is arrested by the Municipal or judicial Police, he shall, within twenty-four hours, exclusive of holidays, be sent to the Courts established under the present Agreement to be dealt with, failing which he shall be released.

ARTICLE V.

The Courts established under the present Agreement shall each have a certain number of procurators to be appointed by the Chinese Government, who shall hold inquests and autopsies (Chien Yen) within the jurisdiction of these Courts and shall otherwise perform their function in accordance with Chinese law in all cases involving the application of Articles 103 to 186 of the Chinese Criminal Code, except where the Municipal Police of the International Settlement or the party concerned has already initiated prosecution, provided that all preliminary investigations conducted by the procurator shall be held publicly and counsel for the accused shall have the right to be present and heard.
In other cases arising within the jurisdiction of the Courts, the Municipal Police or the party concerned shall prosecute. The procurator shall have the right to express his views in court in all criminal cases in which the prosecution is initiated by the Municipal Police or the party concerned.

ARTICLE VI.

All judicial processes, such as summonses, warrants, orders, et cetera, shall be valid only after they have been signed by a judge of the Courts established under the present Agreement, whereupon they shall be served or executed by the judicial police or, as provided below, by the process-servers thereof.
No person found in the International Settlement shall be handed over to the extra-Settlement authorities without a preliminary investigation in court at which counsel for the accused shall have the right to be present and heard, except in the case of requests emanating from other Modern Law Courts when the accused may be handed over after his identity has been established by the Court.
All judgments, decisions and rulings of the Courts shall be executed as soon as they become final as a result of the judicial procedure in force in the said Courts. Whenever necessary, the Municipal Police shall render any assistance within their power as may be requested of them.
The process-servers of the Courts shall be appointed by the Presidents of the Courts respectively and their duties shall be to serve all summonses and deliver other documents of the Courts in connection with civil cases. For the execution of judgments in civil cases, the process-servers shall be accompanied by the judicial police. The officers and members of the judicial police of the Courts shall be appointed by the President of the Branch High Court upon the recommendation of the Municipal Council and shall be subject to dismissal by the President of that Court upon cause shown. Their services will also be terminated by the President at the request of the Municipal Council upon cause shown. They shall wear the uniform designed by the Chinese judicial authorities, and shall be subject to the orders and direction of the Courts and faithful to their duties.

ARTICLE VII.

The House of Detention for civil cases and the Women's Prison attached to the Chinese Court now functioning in the International Settlement at Shanghai shall be transferred from that court to the Courts established under the present Agreement and shall be supervised and administered by the Chinese authorities.
All prisoners now serving sentences in the prisons attached to the Chinese Court now functioning in the International Settlement and those sentenced by the Courts established under the present Agreement shall, at the discretion of the said Courts, serve their sentences either in such prisons in the Settlement or in Chinese prisons outside the Settlement, except that offenders against the Police Offences Code and the Land Regulations and Byelaws and persons under arrest awaiting trial shall serve their periods of detention in the Settlement. The prisons in the Settlement shall be operated, as far as practicable, in conformity with Chinese prison regulations and shall be subject to inspection, from time to time, by officers appointed by the Chinese judicial authorities.
Persons sentenced to death by the Courts established under the present Agreement shall be sent to the Chinese authorities outside of the Settlement for execution of such sentence.

ARTICLE VIII.

Foreign lawyers duly qualified will be admitted to practice in the Courts established under the present Agreement in all cases in which a foreigner is a party, provided such foreign lawyer can only represent the foreign party concerned. The Municipal Council may also be represented in the same manner by duly qualified lawyers, Chinese or foreign, in any proceedings in which the Council is complainant or plaintiff or the Municipal Police is the prosecutor.
In other cases or proceedings in which the Council considers the interests of the Settlement to be involved, it may be represented by a duly qualified lawyer, Chinese or foreign, who may submit to the Court his views in writing during the proceedings and who may, if he deems necessary, file a petition in intervention in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure.
Foreign lawyers who are entitled to practice under this Article in the above-mentioned Courts shall apply to the Ministry of Justice for lawyers' certificates and shall be subject to Chinese laws and regulations applicable to lawyers, including those governing their disciplinary punishment.

ARTICLE IX.

Four permanent representatives shall be appointed, two by the Chinese Government and two by the Governments of the other Powers signatory to the present Agreement, who together shall seek to reconcile such differences of opinion regarding the interpretation or application of the present Agreement as may be referred to them by the President of the Branch High Court or by the authorities of the signatory foreign Powers, provided that their Report shall have no binding force upon either party except by mutual consent, it being understood that no judgments, decisions, rulings or orders of the Courts, as such, shall be referred to the aforesaid representatives for consideration.

ARTICLE X.

The present Agreement and the attached Notes shall enter into effect on April 1st, 1930, and shall continue in force for a period of three years from that date, provided that they may be extended for an additional period upon mutual con-

高等法院分院的判决、裁定和裁决，可根据中国法律向中华民国最高法院上诉。

第三条。

此前领事副手或领事官员出庭观审或会同审案的做法，即在目前于上海公共租界运作的中国法院中的做法，将在根据本协定设立的法院中停止实行。

第四条。

任何人被工部局警察或司法警察逮捕后，应在二十四小时内（节假日除外）送交根据本协定设立的法院处理，否则应予释放。

第五条。

根据本协定设立的各法院应设有若干名检察官，由中国政府任命。检察官应在这些法院的管辖范围内进行验尸和检验（Chien Yen），并在所有涉及适用《中华民国刑法》第103条至第186条的案件中，依照中国法律履行其职能，但工部局警务处或有关当事人已提起公诉的情况除外；前提是检察官进行的所有初步调查均应公开举行，被告辩护律师有权在场并发表意见。
在法院管辖范围内产生的其他案件中，由工部局警务处或有关当事人提起公诉。在所有由工部局警务处或有关当事人提起公诉的刑事案件中，检察官有权在法庭上发表意见。

第六条。

所有司法文书，如传票、逮捕令、命令等，只有经根据本协定设立的法院的法官签署后方为有效，随后由司法警察送达或执行，或如下文规定由法院执达员送达或执行。
在公共租界内发现的任何人，未经法庭初步调查（被告辩护律师有权在场并发表意见），不得移交给租界以外的当局，除非是来自其他现代法律法院的请求，在此情况下，经法院确认被告身份后，可将其移交。
法院的所有判决、裁定和裁决，一经上述法院现行的司法程序使其成为终局判决，即应予以执行。必要时，工部局警务处应在其能力范围内提供所要求的任何协助。
法院执达员由各法院院长分别任命，其职责是送达所有传票并交付与民事案件有关的其他法院文书。在执行民事案件的判决时，执达员应由司法警察陪同。法院司法警察的官员和成员，由高等法院分院院长根据工部局的推荐任命，如有正当理由，可由该法院院长予以免职。如有正当理由，院长也可应工部局的要求终止其职务。他们应穿着由中国司法当局设计的制服，服从法院的命令和指挥，并忠实履行职责。

第七条。

附属于目前在上海公共租界运作的中国法院的民事拘留所和女子监狱，应从该法院移交给根据本协定设立的法院，并由中国当局监督和管理。
目前正在上海公共租界内运作的中国法院附属监狱中服刑的所有囚犯，以及由根据本协定设立的法院判处刑罚的囚犯，可由上述法院酌情决定，在租界内的此类监狱或租界外的中国监狱服刑；但违反《违警律》及《土地章程》和附则的罪犯，以及待审的被捕人员，应在租界内服拘留刑。租界内的监狱应在可行范围内按照中国监狱规章运作，并应接受由中国司法当局任命的官员不时进行的视察。
由根据本协定设立的法院判处死刑的人，应送往租界外的中国当局执行该刑罚。

第八条。

在有外国人作为当事人的所有案件中，允许具备正式资格的外国律师在根据本协定设立的法院执业，但该外国律师只能代理有关的外国当事人。在工部局为控告人或原告、或工部局警务处为公诉人的任何诉讼程序中，工部局也可由具备正式资格的华人或外国律师以同样方式代表。
在工部局认为涉及租界利益的其他案件或程序中，工部局可由具备正式资格的华人或外国律师代表，该律师可在诉讼过程中向法院提交书面意见，并可在认为必要时，依照《民事诉讼法》的规定提出介入诉讼的申请。
有权根据本条在上述法院执业的外国律师，应向司法部申请律师证书，并受适用于律师的中国法律法规的约束，包括有关纪律惩处的法规。

第九条。

应任命四名常任代表，其中两名由中国政府任命，两名由本协定其他签字国政府任命，他们共同致力于调和由高等法院分院院长或签字外国当局提交给他们的、关于本协定解释或适用的意见分歧；前提是，除非双方同意，否则他们的报告对任何一方均无约束力；并需明确理解，法院本身的任何判决、裁定、裁决或命令，不得提交给上述代表审议。

第十条。

本协定及所附照会应于1930年4月1日生效，并从该日起继续有效三年，但经双方同
