April 16, 1937. Morning Translation.

National Herald and other local newspapers :-

ABOLITION OF CONSULAR JURISDICTION

The Shanghai First Special District Citizens'
Federation yesterday sent the following telegraphic petition
to Dr. Wang Chung-hui, Minister of Foreign Affairs:-
"At the end of the Ching Dynasty, various
nations forced our country to sign unequal treaties with
them by virtue of which they are allowed to exercise consular
jurisdiction in China. Besides impairing the judicial rights
of China, this system has become a shield for unscrupulous
foreign residents who frequently commit unlawful acts thereby
endangering Chinese lives and property and disturbing public
peace and order.
"China is now a united nation and her judicial
system has been made adequate; therefore the various foreign
nations can have no reason for maintaining consular jurisdic-
tion. For the sake of our liberty and equality, we should
unhesitatingly declare this system null and void. The
abolition of consular jurisdiction in Egypt will be put into
effect soon. Are we inferior even to Egypt?
"It is our hope that you will, in accordance
with the resolution passed at the Third Plenary Session and
in compliance with the earnest desire of the people, declare
the consular jurisdiction enjoyed by various nations in
China as abolished forthwith."

Shanghai Bar Association to Convene Meeting of Public
Bodies

The Executive and Supervisory Committees of the
Shanghai Bar Association held a meeting at 6 p.m. yesterday,
at which Mr. Fang Tsing-jih (方俊傑) presided. A report
was made to the effect that letters had been received from
the Chinese Ratepayers' Association of the International
Settlement, the General Labour Union, the Chung Hwa
Vocational Education Society and other public bodies
supporting the proposal of the Bar Association to abolish
consular jurisdiction.
The following resolution was passed :-
"Mr. Loh Ting-kuei (陸鼎揆), member, as
suggested that a Consular Jurisdiction Abolition
Movement be launched in conjunction with various public
bodies.
"Resolved: that a Consular Jurisdiction
Abolition Movement Meeting be held in conjunction with
various public bodies; that Messrs. Loh Ting-kuei,
Zing Lien-kwei (秦聯奎), Sung Tsu-kyi (孫祖基),
Chang Ping-chuen (張秉銓) and Chang Chueh-sung (張覺聲),
committee members, be appointed to make preparations
for the meeting."

废除领事裁判权

上海第一特区市民联合会昨日向外交部长王宠惠博士发出如下电报请愿：-
“清朝末年，各国强迫我国与其签订不平等条约，据此允许其在中国行使领事裁判权。该制度除损害中国司法权外，还成为不法外籍居民的护身符，他们频繁实施违法行为，从而危及中国人的生命财产，扰乱公共和平与秩序。

中国记者协会举行会议

在本地中国记者协会执行委员会和监察委员会成员分别于4月10日和13日举行的会议上，讨论并通过了以下决议：-

(1) 鉴于上海律师公会书面请求支持废除领事裁判权运动，指示本会秘书处复函律师公会，保证本会一致支持该运动。

(2) 由本会监察委员张季平先生提议，向组成赴日本及“满洲国”考察团的天津记者发出警告。

决议由本会发表宣言，谴责该团体的行动。

April 17, 1937. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers:-

ABOLITION OF CONSULAR JURISDICTION

The abolition of the consular jurisdiction enjoyed by the various nations in China has become the unanimous demand of the Chinese people. The various local public bodies are making preparations to form a "Consular Jurisdiction Abolition Association" to study the question.

Yesterday the Chinese Ratepayers' Association in the International Settlement sent a reply to the Shanghai Bar Association pledging its support of the suggestion made by Mr. Loh Ting-kwei ( 陸 鼎 揆 ), a member of the Bar Association, for the abolition of the consular jurisdiction. In its reply, the Ratepayers' Association also quoted the gist of telegrams sent on May 14, July 10 and November 28, 1929, to Dr. C.T. Wang, the then Minister of Foreign Affairs, pointing out to him the evil effects of the consular jurisdiction on the judicial system of China and the unlawful activities, such as gambling, dog-racing, trafficking in opium and firearms, then indulged in by unscrupulous foreigners in Shanghai who were immune from interference by the Chinese authorities by virtue of the consular jurisdiction they were enjoying.

At a meeting of the Executive and Supervisory Committee of the Shanghai Medical Practitioners' Association held yesterday with Mr. Chu Niang-kao ( 朱 仰 高 ) in the chair, it was resolved that the proposal of the Shanghai Bar Association to abolish consular jurisdiction in China be supported.

废除领事裁判权

废除各国在华享有的领事裁判权已成为中国人民的一致要求。各地公共团体正在筹备成立“废除领事裁判权协会”，以研究此问题。

昨日，国际租界华人纳税会复函上海律师公会，承诺支持该公会会员陆鼎揆先生提出的废除领事裁判权的建议。纳税会在复函中还引用了1929年5月14日、7月10日和11月28日发给时任外交部长王正廷博士的电报要点，向他指出领事裁判权对中国司法制度的恶劣影响，以及在上海的不法外籍人士凭借其所享有的领事裁判权免受中国当局干涉，从而从事赌博、赛狗、贩卖鸦片和枪支等非法活动。

在昨日举行的上海医师公会执行委员会和监察委员会会议上，由朱仰高先生主持，决议支持上海律师公会关于废除在华领事裁判权的提议。

April 18, 1937. Morning Translation.

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

ABOLITION OF CONSULAR JURISDICTION

The Nanking Road Street Union and the
First Branch of the Shanghai First Special District Citizens'
Federation yesterday sent the following telegraphic
petition to Dr. Wang Chung-hui, Minister of Foreign Affairs,
in connection with the question of the abolition of
consular jurisdiction:-
"Many unlawful activities, such as smuggling
in firearms, traffic in drugs, establishment of gambling
dens, etc. which have done considerable harm to the Chinese
people, to say nothing of their adverse effects upon the
peace and order of the community, have been engaged in
by unscrupulous foreign nationals residing in China because
of the existence of the consular jurisdiction which they
enjoy and which makes them immune from interference by
the Chinese authorities. In former times, the foreign
nations may have been unwilling to give up this privilege
under the pretext that the Chinese judicial system was
not up to standard, but this cannot be the case now in
view of the great improvement in our judicial system.
If they did not entertain any ulterior motives, the Powers
would not be unwilling to give up this privilege. In case
of failure to bring about the abolition of this system
through negotiations, we request you to do your utmost
to declare independently the abolition of this unequal
jurisdiction with a view to upholding our national rights."

National Herald and other local newspapers :-

CITIZENS' FEDERATION REQUESTS STRENGTHENING OF CUSTOMS
PREVENTIVE UNITS

The Shanghai First Special District Citizens'
Federation yesterday sent the following telegraphic petition
to the Ministry of Finance:-
"Smuggled Japanese goods are continuing
to flood the markets everywhere. It is unnecessary to
mention the conditions in North China. Even in Shanghai,
smuggled goods have been seized on several occasions during
the past month and Customs officers have been assaulted
and injured by armed ronins who undertook the transportation
of smuggled goods. It is only due to the unwavering
spirit of the Customs officials and their unceasing efforts
at preventing the smuggling that smugglers have become
less bold than before.
"The smuggling not only affects the Customs
revenue, but is a serious menace to our national industries
and commerce. Unless a stop is put to the smuggling
immediately, our Customs law will be useless and the people
will go bankrupt.
"You are requested to order the Customs
authorities throughout the country to strengthen their
preventive units so as to eradicate smuggling."

《民报》及当地其他报纸：-

废除领事裁判权

南京路街联会和上海第一特区市民联合会第一分会昨日就废除领事裁判权问题，向外交部长王宠惠博士发出如下电请愿书：-
“许多非法活动，如走私枪支、贩毒、开设赌场等，不仅严重危害中国人民，更对社区和平秩序产生不利影响，这些活动均由在华居住的不法外籍人士所为，原因是他们享有领事裁判权，使其免受中国当局干涉。过去，各国可能以中国司法制度未达标准为借口，不愿放弃这一特权，但鉴于我国司法制度的巨大进步，如今已非如此。若列强无任何 ulterior motives（原文不清/别有用心），不会不愿放弃这一特权。若通过谈判未能实现废除该制度，恳请阁下竭尽全力，单方面宣布废除这种不平等管辖权，以维护我国国权。”

《国民日报》及当地其他报纸：-

市民联合会请求加强海关缉私队

上海第一特区市民联合会昨日向财政部发出如下电请愿书：-
“走私日货继续充斥各地市场。华北情况自不待言。即使在上海，上月也多次查获走私货物，负责运输走私货物的武装浪人袭击并打伤海关官员。仅因海关官员坚定的精神和不懈的缉私努力，走私者才不如以前大胆。
“走私不仅影响关税收入，而且对我国民族工商业构成严重威胁。若不立即制止走私，我国海关法将形同虚设，人民将破产。
“恳请命令全国海关当局加强缉私队，以根除走私。”

April 20, 1937. Afternoon Translation

Here, we wish to reiterate what we have said before:
"By virtue of consular jurisdiction, Japan has permitted her
ronins to violate our laws, rob our revenues, poison our
people, spy on our national defensive schemes and commit
acts of lawlessness wherever they go." The original reason
for introducing consular jurisdiction was to protect the
right, whereas to-day it is being used as a weapon to destroy
the right. If the European and American citizens would
think of their interests in China which are being shattered
by the lawless activities of a brutal force, they would
realize that it is a foolish act to bind China by consular
jurisdiction.
We would like to assure the Powers that China is
now an independent nation and that she is fully aware of
how to deal with her enemy and to discharge her obligations
to those friendly Powers who treat her on the basis of
equality.

在此，我们要重申我们之前说过的话：
“凭借领事裁判权，日本允许其浪人违反我国法律，掠夺我国税收，毒害我国人民，刺探我国国防计划，并在所到之处犯下无法无天之罪行。”引入领事裁判权的初衷是为了保护权利，而今天它却被用作破坏权利的武器。如果欧美公民想到他们在华利益正被一股残暴力量的非法活动所粉碎，他们就会意识到用领事裁判权束缚中国是一个愚蠢的行为。
我们要向列强保证，中国现在是一个独立的国家，完全知道如何对付敌人，以及如何履行对那些以平等 basis（基础）对待她的友好国家的义务。

Tientsin, Shanghai, Hankow and Canton, and a number of foreign
lawyers engaged to give opinions during the hearing of cases
involving foreigners, but they were not to be allowed to
interfere with the judgment. This is also a transitional

The establishment of Special Courts would cause
great inconvenience. China has many commercial treaty ports

Furthermore, the presence of foreign lawyers in the Special

are of the opinion that after the abolition of consular

China Evening News of April 19 published the following editorial
comment :-

Advice to Powers Concerned on the Question of Abolition
of Consular Jurisdiction

The introduction of consular jurisdiction is a means
of self-defence by a country more advanced in civilization
towards a backward nation and is also a sign of the instability
of the political organization of the nation where it exists.
However, we wish the Powers concerned to consider carefully
whether or not the political machine of China to-day is able
to protect foreign nationals and whether or not the laws of
China are able to accord them reasonable security. There
are a great number of foreign nationals now being afforded
protection by China's laws, among whom are Germans, Soviet
Russians, etc. No complaints have been received from these
foreigners of harsh treatment. On the contrary, owing to
the consular jurisdiction in force, sometimes public officers
of irregular police forces, such as those in the Police
Stations in the Settlement, ignore the orders of the Chinese
tribunals and commit unlawful acts such as the infliction of
torture when examining suspects. This renders the Chinese
people unable to enjoy the protection afforded by their own
laws. The existence of consular jurisdiction is oppressing
the Chinese people even in their own country. We sincerely
hope that foreigners will cast off their prejudice by thinking
over this problem as if they were Chinese people. It was
reported in the newspapers that two American ladies wished
to give up their nationality and to be naturalized as Chinese
citizens. They said that they did so as a protest against
the desire of their own government to retain consular
jurisdiction. We trust that there are a great number of
fair-minded persons in America and Europe who entertain the
same ideas as these two American ladies.

有人建议在北平、天津、上海、汉口和广州设立特别法庭，并聘请若干外国律师在涉及外国人的案件审理期间提供意见，但不允许他们干涉判决。这也是一种过渡措施，比暹罗和埃及采取的措施保留了更多的主权。自民国十年以来，中国与各国签订了新协定，俄罗斯、德国、芬兰、波兰等许多国家已放弃其领事裁判权。中国对外籍居民的审判是公正的。实际上，中国并不需要过渡措施。
设立特别法庭会造成极大不便。中国有许多通商口岸，将所有涉及外国人的案件都带到上述五个特别法庭会引起许多抱怨。此外，外国律师出现在特别法庭并不意味着完全平等。无论如何，我们认为，在废除领事裁判权之后、设立特别法庭之前，不应允许外国人在全国范围内自由行动。

4月19日《China Evening News》（《中国晚报》，音译）发表了以下社论评论：-

就废除领事裁判权问题向有关列强进言

引入领事裁判权是文明较先进国家对落后国家的一种自卫手段，也是存在该制度的国家政治组织不稳定的标志。然而，我们希望有关列强仔细考虑，当今中国的政治机器是否能够保护外籍人士，以及中国法律是否能够给予他们合理的安全保障。目前有大量外籍人士受到中国法律的保护，其中包括德国人、苏联俄国人等。这些外国人并未投诉受到虐待。相反，由于现行领事裁判权的存在，有时像租界巡捕房这样的非正规警察队伍的公职人员无视中国法庭的命令，在审讯嫌疑人时实施酷刑等非法行为。这使得中国人民无法享受自己法律提供的保护。领事裁判权的存在甚至在中国本土压迫着中国人民。我们真诚希望外国人能设身处地，像中国人一样思考这个问题，从而抛弃偏见。据报纸报道，两位美国女士希望放弃国籍，归化为中国公民。她们表示，这样做是为了抗议本国政府保留领事裁判权的意愿。我们相信，在欧美有大量秉持公正理念的人持有与这两位美国女士相同的想法。

April 20, 1937.
4
No. D
Afternoon Translation 1/7

Sin Wen Pao publishes the following editorial comment :-

A STUDY OF THE QUESTION OF ABOLITION OF CONSULAR
JURISDICTION

Of late, public attention has been drawn to
the question of the abolition of consular jurisdiction.
Leading local organizations are suggesting the convocation
of public representatives to organize a Committee to study
the question of the abolition of consular jurisdiction.
The following are our views on this question :-
The Europeans first extended their jurisdiction
to foreign countries in the near East and later to the Far
Eastern countries. A few years ago Japan secured the
removal of this special foreign privilege and she was
followed by Burma, Turkey and Iran. Now, Egypt is taking
a similar step. China is at present the only country in
the East which cannot rid herself of the system. However,
China is rich in resources; her teeming population and
busy markets are sufficient to affect world prosperity.
She cannot be compared with any other country in the Near
or Far East. If the advanced Powers still adhere to
their established narrow-minded views by maintaining such
an obsolete system, it means that they still regard China
as less important than Turkey, Iran and Siam. This not
only lowers the self-respect of the 400,000,000 Chinese
people, but it also loosens the tie of national friendliness
brought into being through 90 years of commercial relations.
We are confident that the far-sighted politicians of the
various Powers will not be led astray by public opinion
but the success of this matter depends entirely on our own
endeavours.
The abolition of consular jurisdiction came
dearly to Siam, but Japan obtained it otherwise; she simply
cancelled the limit of residential areas for foreigners in
the eight ports and opened the whole country free for the
residence and commerce of foreigners. This is the natural
course because commercial ports are the special products
of the system of consular jurisdiction which prevents the
opening up of the whole country. When consular jurisdiction
is no more, aliens will receive similar legal treatment to
our own countrymen; the limitation of residential areas for
foreign people will, under the circumstances, be unnecessary.
The treaties arranged during the Ching Dynasty between
China and Great Britain, America and Japan have not been
altered, but the renewed Sino-Belgian, Sino-Italian, Sino-
Portuguese and Sino-Spanish commercial treaties have been
supplemented with a declaration that the people of the
countries concerned can reside, transact business and enjoy
land possession rights in any part of the treaty countries.
This step follows the precedent of Japan in her removal of
consular jurisdiction. In future, when the question of
abolition is settled, the various Powers concerned will
all be given the same facilities.
Siam adopted a gradual process in abolishing
consular jurisdiction. In the Siamese Courts, the first
and second trials are to be participated in during hearing
by foreign judges; while the Consular Courts still reserve
the right to ask for transfer of prisoners for trial.
Egypt is adopting a transitional measure by abolishing
the consular Courts while retaining the Mixed Court system.

《新闻报》发表如下社论：-

废除领事裁判权问题之研究

近来，公众注意力被吸引到废除领事裁判权的问题上。本地主要团体建议召集公众代表，组织一个委员会来研究废除领事裁判权的问题。以下是我们对此问题的看法：-
欧洲人首先将其管辖权扩展到近东国家，随后扩展到远东国家。几年前，日本成功废除了这一外国特权，缅甸、土耳其和伊朗紧随其后。如今，埃及也采取了类似的步骤。中国目前是东方唯一无法摆脱该制度的国家。然而，中国资源丰富；其众多的人口和繁忙的市场足以影响世界繁荣。她不能与近东或远东的任何其他国家相提并论。如果先进列强仍坚持其既定的狭隘观点，维持这种过时的制度，那就意味着他们仍将中国看得比土耳其、伊朗和暹罗（泰国）次要。这不仅降低了四亿中国人民的自尊，也松动了通过90年商业关系建立起来的国家友好纽带。我们相信，各列强有远见的政治家不会被舆论引入歧途，但此事的成功完全取决于我们自身的努力。
暹罗废除领事裁判权付出了高昂代价，但日本则以另一种方式获得；她 simply 取消了八个通商口岸外国人居住区的限制，并向外国人的居住和商业全面开放全国。这是自然的进程，因为通商口岸是领事裁判权制度的特殊产物，该制度阻碍了全国的开放。当领事裁判权不复存在时，外国人将受到与我国同胞相同的法律待遇；在这种情况下，限制外国人居住区已无必要。
清朝时期中国与英国、美国和日本签订的条约尚未更改，但新签订的中比、中意、中葡和中西商业条约已补充声明，有关国家人民可在条约国的任何地区居住、经商并享有土地所有权。这一步骤遵循了日本废除领事裁判权的先例。将来，当废除问题得到解决时，各有关列强都将获得同样的便利。
暹罗在废除领事裁判权方面采取了渐进的过程。在暹罗法院，初审和二审期间将有外国法官参与听审；而领事法院仍保留要求移交囚犯受审的权利。埃及正采取过渡措施，废除领事法院，同时保留混合法庭制度。在王正廷博士担任中国外交部长期间

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

CHINESE RATEPAYERS' ASSOCIATION OF FRENCH CONCESSION
DESIRES ABOLITION OF CONSULAR JURISDICTION

At a meeting held at 4 p.m. yesterday by
the Chinese Ratepayers' Association of the French Concession,
which was presided over by Mr. Mau Yung (毛 雲), the
following resolutions were discussed and passed:-
(1) That the French Municipal Council be
requested to bring up immediately for further consideration
the question of licence fees for servants' employment
agencies with a view to reduction.
(2) That a telegraphic petition be despatched
to Dr. Wang Chung-hui, Minister of Foreign Affairs,
demanding the abolition of consular jurisdiction.
The petition was sent out yesterday and in
it Dr. Wang Chung-hui, Minister of Foreign Affairs, was
urged to do his utmost in compliance with the doctrines
of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen to bring about the abolition
of this antiquated system as a preliminary measure
for the cancellation of all unequal treaties.

Ambassador to U.S.A. Urged to Press for Abolition

Dr. C.T. Wang, the newly appointed Chinese
Ambassador to the United States, was entertained at a
tea-party given by more than 60 local public bodies,
including the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, the Chinese
Ratepayers' Associations of the International Settlement
and the French Concession, the local Tangpu, etc., at
5 p.m. yesterday at the Park Hotel, Bubbling Well Road,
on his impending departure for his new post.
In the course of his speech, Mr. Wong Shiao-
lai, Chairman of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, urged
Dr. C.T. Wang to endeavour to bring about the approval
of the United States Government for China's desire for
the abolition of consular jurisdiction.

Educational Association Pledges Support

At a meeting held yesterday by the Shanghai
Municipality Educational Association, which was presided
over by Mr. Huang Chao-yung (黃 造 雄), it was resolved
that unanimous support be pledged to the Shanghai Bar
Association in connection with its proposal for the
abolition of the consular jurisdiction enjoyed by the
various foreign nations in China.

Abolition Committee Meeting to be Held To-Morrow

The Consular Jurisdiction Abolition Movement
Committee, promoted by the Shanghai Bar Association, will
hold its first meeting at 5 p.m. on Wednesday, April 21,
at the office of the Association, No. 30 Rue Cornille,
French Concession.

法租界华人纳税会希望废除领事裁判权

在昨天下午4时举行的法租界华人纳税会会议上，由毛雲先生主持，讨论并通过了以下决议：-
(1) 请求公董局立即重新审议佣工介绍所执照费问题，以期降低费用。
(2) 向外交部长王宠惠博士发出电报请愿，要求废除领事裁判权。
该请愿书已于昨日发出，其中敦促外交部长王宠惠博士竭尽全力，遵照已故孙中山博士的遗教，废除这一过时制度，作为取消所有不平等条约的初步措施。

敦促驻美大使推动废除

新任中国驻美大使王正廷博士，昨日午后5时在静安寺路国际饭店举行的茶会上受到款待，出席者包括上海总商会、公共租界及法租界华人纳税会、本地党部等六十多个本地公共团体，以此为他即将赴任新职送行。
上海总商会主席王晓籁先生在演讲中，敦促王正廷博士努力争取美国政府批准中国废除领事裁判权的愿望。

教育协会承诺支持

在昨天举行的上海市教育协会会议上，由黃造雄先生主持，会议决定一致支持上海律师公会关于废除各国在华享有的领事裁判权的提议。

废除委员会将于明日举行会议

由上海律师公会发起的废除领事裁判权运动委员会，将于4月21日（星期三）下午5时在该会办事处（法租界高乃伊路30号）举行第一次会议。

Lih Pao publishes the following articles:

ABOLITION OF CONSULAR JURISDICTION IN RELATION TO LABOUR
TROUBLES

The workers of the Shanghai Electric Construction
Company have now been on strike three times. On each
occasion, the management of the company has declared that
negotiations over the necessary demands would be opened
after the strikers had resumed work. About three months
have elapsed since the first strike, yet due to the
insincerity of the management, the demands submitted by
the workers have not been accepted. This adamant attitude
on the part of the management of the company has caused
repeated inconvenience to the citizens as well as a menace
to the peace and order of the community. The matter
should be dealt with by arbitration according to law.
It seems that the movement to abolish consular
jurisdiction in Egypt has not had much effect on the minds
of the Chinese people. Although there are persons
suggesting the abolition of consular jurisdiction in China,
yet they have not propagated the reasons for the abolition
among the masses so as to bring about an extensive movement.
A movement of the people to abolish consular jurisdiction
is very necessary, because after abolition is attained,
any dispute such as a strike of tramway workers, will be
dealt with by the Labour-Capital Disputes Arbitration
Office according to the Labour Law.
Above all, the aim of the Chinese people should
be to effect the rendition of the Foreign Settlements.

The Hwa Mei Chao Pao (華美早報):

CHIEF OF OPIUM SUPPRESSION INSPECTORATE TO ASSUME DUTY

Mr. Hsu Tung-yung (徐統雄), the chief of the local

Eastern Times and other local newspapers :-

TWO DETECTIVES OF POLICE BUREAU CHARGED WITH TORTURE

Two Chinese detectives named Ho Wen-ching (何文錦)
and Koo Tsing-ching (顧俊卿), attached to the Shanghai City
Government Police Bureau Headquarters and the West Gate
Branch Bureau respectively, are due to appear in the Shanghai
District Court, Nankiao, to-day to face charges of deprivation
of personal freedom and assault brought by one Vai Sz-hsi
(萬如喜).
Vai Sz-hsi and another named Vai Siao-zung-ts
(萬小成子) were arrested on suspicion of having stolen 50
bags of wheat from the Sung Dah Flour Mill (宋大麵粉廠) on
February 9 this year. It is alleged that during the time
the arrested men were detained, the two detectives applied
tortures to Vai Sz-hsi in an attempt to force a confession
from him, thereby causing him bodily harm.

《立报》发表以下文章：

废除领事裁判权与劳资纠纷的关系

上海电力建设公司的工人目前已罢工三次。每次公司管理层都宣布，在罢工者复工后将就必要诉求展开谈判。自第一次罢工以来已过去约三个月，但由于管理层缺乏诚意，工人提出的诉求未被接受。公司管理层的这种强硬态度给市民带来了反复的不便，并对社区的和平与秩序构成威胁。此事应依法通过仲裁处理。
似乎埃及废除领事裁判权的运动对中国民众的思想影响不大。虽然有人建议在中国废除领事裁判权，但他们并未在群众中宣传废除的理由，以促成广泛的运动。民众废除领事裁判权的运动是非常必要的，因为一旦实现废除，任何诸如电车工人罢工的纠纷，都将由劳资争议仲裁处根据《劳动法》进行处理。
最重要的是，中国人民的目标应是实现收回外国租界。

April 28, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

Min Pao and other local newspapers:-

FELLOW-COUNTRYMEN'S ASSOCIATION DEMAND ABOLITION OF
CONSULATE JURISDICTION

More than fifty local fellow-countrymen's associa-
tions, including the Kwangtung, the Ningpo, the Shaoshing and
the Chinkiang Fellow Countrymen's Associations, yesterday
submitted a joint petition to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
demanding the independent abolition of consular jurisdiction.
The petition points out how unscrupulous elements among the
foreign nationals have, taking advantage of this unjust
privilege which they enjoy, engaged themselves in such
unlawful activities as traffic in narcotic drugs and firearms,
smuggling, etc. which not only affect our national revenue
but also constitute a serious menace to the peace and order
of the country.

The petition urges the Minister of Foreign Affairs
to declare fearlessly the independent abolition of this
antiquated system in compliance with the will of the late
Dr. Sun Yat-sen as well as with the decisions reached at
the Third Plenary Session, so as to uphold the unification
of our judicial system.

Ta Mei Wan Pao :-

ABOLITION OF CONSULAR JURISDICTION DESIRED

Since the Chinese Ratepayers' Association brought up the question of abolition of consular jurisdiction, people in various circles in this locality have responded and formed the Consular Jurisdiction Abolition Research Society to study measures to effect the abolition.
On May 1, our reporter called on Mr. Chen Vee-van (陳維藩) of the Chinese Ratepayers' Association, who made the following statement :- "The Consular Jurisdiction Abolition Research Society is studying measures and procedure to bring about the abolition. The position of China in the world has been raised, but due to interference by the "friendly nation", it is difficult to attain the abolition of consular jurisdiction. In my view, the Chinese Government may automatically announce abolition of consular jurisdiction. Efforts are being made to make arrangements with various local public bodies to request the Government to announce the abolition."

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

MEETING OF THE CITIZENS' FEDERATION

At 2 p.m. yesterday, the 21st Branch of the First Special District Citizens' Federation held an election of new executive committeemen for the ensuing year. As a result, Messrs Yih Chia-shing (叶家兴), Ma Ying-liang (马荫良), Wang Pah-ji (汪伯奇) and ten others were appointed to serve on the Executive Committee of the Branch.
The following resolutions were then discussed and passed :-
1) Every afternoon, a large number of beggars appear in Chow Ching Li (曹家里), near Shanse Road, between Kiujiang and Hankow Roads, and force merchants to give them money. Customers are afraid to go there and this affects the business of the shops. Measures should be devised to put a stop to this.
Resolved: that the S.M.C. be requested to suppress the beggars for the sake of the merchants.
2) That steps be taken to effect a reduction of house rentals in Chow Ching Li, near Shanse Road.
3) That the increase of the Municipal Rate by the S.M.C. be opposed.
4) That the Citizens' Federation be requested to send a petition to the National Government asking for the abolition of consular jurisdiction.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

CHINESE BOY INJURED DURING JAPANESE MANOEUVRES : MEDICAL EXPENSES GIVEN

At 9 a.m. May 1, the Japanese marines held manoeuvres along Kiangwan Road, during which hand grenades were thrown. Chui Ping-tao (崔炳道), 12-year-old son of Chui Miao-sung (崔妙松), a carpenter living in Lane 41, No. 1, Tung Chi Road, was hit in the forehead and began to bleed. The Japanese marines sent a doctor to treat the injured boy and medical expenses were also paid.

3) Regarding the statement that this matter will tend to
arouse the displeasure of various friendly Powers who
have recently arrived at better relations with China
through diplomatic efforts, I maintain that this point
is not proven. Of course, foreigners in Shanghai
regard consular jurisdiction as of the utmost
importance, but in the eyes of diplomats in Washington,
London, Paris and Rome, it is not so vital. When I
was present as a newspaper reporter at the Washington
Conference, the various Powers hesitated on this
question when it was put up for discussion; they did
not show a definite attitude simply because their
knowledge of the Far Eastern situation was not complete.
The fear that we may annoy the various Powers by taking
such action is baseless; such unnecessary fear lowers
our national prestige. The more we are in danger,
the braver we should be. We should let the world
know that we are not submissive. Such a spirit will
produce a magnificent effect.
4) Regarding the procedure to be used, I still adhere to
the view that independent action should be taken.
Only thus will the movement be effective. If we
consult on the matter with the various Powers, bargaining
will take place with the result that many terms for
settlement will be made and we will still not attain
our object. The negotiations in Egypt on the same
subject resulted in the establishment of a mixed
court system and complete abolition of consular
jurisdiction was not attained. If China brings the
matter up for discussion with the various Powers
concerned, these latter will naturally use the same
measures as in the case of Egypt. It will be
undignified for China to be treated as a vassal state.
The only way open to us is to present our intention to
the Powers with the remark that, as they were free to
cancel certain treaties such as the war debt agreement,
the Versailles Treaty etc., we are entitled to act
likewise. Only by this method can we arrive quickly
at abolition and the Powers concerned will be unable
to protest.
5) The Tokyo Government has expressed its sympathy towards
Chinese demands for the abolition of consular jurisdiction
but it considers that the period before abolition
should depend on the degree of development made in the
Chinese judicial system. In my opinion, such an
argument was correct in former days when Chinese
judicial codes were not complete and courts were few.
Now, China has complete judicial codes and courts are
established everywhere; the Powers concerned can find
no more excuses for holding their extrality. As for
the question of the degree of improvement in the Chinese
judiciary, according to my experience gained in practising
law in foreign countries, I dare say that in any country,
even one with a long judicial history, can be found many
defects in the legal system used. There are short-
comings in all systems and not a single country in the

3) 关于此举倾向于引起最近通过外交努力与中国改善关系的各友好强国不满的说法，我认为这一点未经证实。当然，在上海的外国人视领事裁判权为至关重要，但在华盛顿、伦敦、巴黎和罗马的外交官眼中，它并非如此生死攸关。当我作为新闻记者出席华盛顿会议时，各国在这一问题被提出讨论时犹豫不决；他们未表现出明确态度，仅仅是因为他们对远东局势的了解并不全面。担心我们采取此类行动会惹恼各强国是毫无根据的；这种不必要的恐惧降低了我们的国家威望。我们越处于危险之中，就越应该勇敢。我们应该让世界知道我们并不顺从。这种精神将产生巨大的效果。
4) 关于所采用的程序，我仍然坚持应采取独立行动的观点。只有这样才能使运动有效。如果我们就此问题与各强国协商，就会发生讨价还价，导致达成许多和解条款，而我们仍无法达到目标。埃及就同一主题进行的谈判导致了混合法庭制度的建立，并未实现领事裁判权的完全废除。如果中国与有关各强国提出讨论此事，后者自然会采取与埃及案例相同的措施。中国被当作附庸国对待是有失体面的。我们要走的唯一道路是向列强表明我们的意图，并指出，既然他们可以自由取消某些条约，如战债协定、凡尔赛条约等，我们也有权采取同样的行动。只有通过这种方法，我们才能迅速实现废除，而有关列强将无法提出抗议。
5) 东京政府对中国废除领事裁判权的要求表示同情，但它认为废除前的过渡期应取决于中国司法体系的发展程度。在我看来，这种论点在中国法典尚不完备、法院寥寥无几的过去是正确的。如今，中国拥有完备的法典，各地均设立了法院；有关列强再也找不到保留其治外法权的借口。至于中国司法改进程度的问题，根据我在国外从事法律工作的经验，我敢说，在任何国家，即使是拥有悠久司法历史的国家，其使用的法律制度中也能发现许多缺陷。所有制度都有缺点，世界上没有一个国家的

LAWYER LOH TING-KWEI'S VIEWS REGARDING THE ABOLITION
OF CONSULAR JURISDICTION

The following are the views of Lawyer Loh Ting-
Kwei (陸鼎揆) on the question of the abolition of
consular jurisdictions:-
"Since I proposed the independent abolition of
consular jurisdiction, after the precedent set by the Allied
Powers in suspending war debt payment, and by Germany in
her individual action of abolishing the Paris Treaty, wide
approval has been voiced by our countrymen. This shows
that the people throughout the country have long had a
similar desire. The Shanghai Bar Association is now
accelerating the matter among the various public bodies.
In view of the great importance of this question, detailed
discussions should be held in order to avert future
obstructions.
"Regarding this question, certain persons are of the
opinion that, although it is one of the most important
political matters, there are for the time being some other
national questions which are more important. In their
opinion, diplomatic dealings with Japan should be placed
above all other questions, and no matters of minor importance
should be taken up to divert the public attention. They
say that at the present juncture when we are experiencing
great difficulty in dealing with Japan, the putting up of
the question of the abolition of consular jurisdiction will
mean aggravation of our difficulties as we will have to
deal with many Powers instead of with one. Furthermore,
this question will affect the good feelings of various
Powers towards us.
"I regard the above arguments as beneficial
to the through study of this question, but in my view,
they can be met as follows:-
1) It shows excessive anxiety to imagine that the raising
of the consular jurisdiction abolition question will
divert public attention from national problems of a
more important nature. In every country, there are
many civil and foreign questions which are equal in
importance. The Government and the people should fix
their minds on all and every one of them at the same
time. It is irrational to say that the attention
given to other matters will be lessened when one single
question is taken up. The people are not so simple
as to forget other important national affairs when their
attention is directed at the abolition of consular
jurisdiction.
2) Owing to the present situation, some people consider
that this question is not so important as others such as
national defence, finance etc. It must be understood
that these latter questions have much to do with the
extraterritorial system. If no fundamental settlement
is made to remove the system, judicial rights cannot be
fully exercised within our own territory, and financial
administration will be constantly handicapped, while
thorough preparations for national defence will be

陆鼎揆律师关于废除领事裁判权的观点

以下是陆鼎揆律师关于废除领事裁判权问题的观点：
“自从我参照协约国暂停偿还战债以及德国单方面废除巴黎条约的先例，提出独立废除领事裁判权以来，得到了同胞们的广泛赞同。这表明全国民众长期以来一直有类似的愿望。上海律师公会目前正在各公共团体中加速推进此事。鉴于这一问题的重要性，应进行详细讨论，以避免未来的阻碍。
“关于这个问题，有些人认为，虽然这是最重要的政治事项之一，但目前还有一些其他的国家问题更为重要。在他们看来，对日外交应置于所有其他问题之上，不应处理次要事项以分散公众注意力。他们说，在目前我们对日交涉面临巨大困难的关头，提出废除领事裁判权的问题意味着加剧我们的困难，因为我们将不得不应对多个强国，而不是仅仅一个。此外，这个问题会影响各强国对我们的好感。
“我认为上述论点有利于对这一问题进行深入研究，但在我看来，可以如下回应：
1) 想象提出废除领事裁判权问题会分散公众对更重要国家问题的注意力，是过度焦虑的表现。在每个国家，都有许多同等重要的内政和外交问题。政府和民众应同时关注每一个问题。说当提出一个单一问题时，对其他事项的关注就会减少，这是不合逻辑的。民众并不那么简单，不会因为关注废除领事裁判权而忘记其他重要的国家事务。
2) 由于目前的局势，有些人认为这个问题不如国防、财政等其他问题重要。必须明白，后一些问题与治外法权制度有很大关系。如果不从根本上解决以消除该制度，我们就无法在自己的领土内充分行使司法权，财政管理将不断受到阻碍，而彻底的国防准备也将

Crystal (晶報):

COMPULSORY SALE OF TOILET PAPER

It seems that the public lavatories in
the Foreign Settlements of Shanghai are too few. Citizens
in general often suffer much inconvenience, not so much
through the small number of public lavatories, but through
the compulsory selling of toilet paper by the coolies who
take charge of them. We have on many occasions been
very indignant over and disgusted at the action of these
coolies in forcibly selling toilet paper at two or three
coppers per sheet, but when we read the report of the
contractors of various public lavatories to the effect
that the S.M.C. has interfered in their selling of toilet
paper despite the fact that they have paid to the Council
a large amount of money for the contracts, we cannot
but withhold our blame from these contractors. As the
establishment of public lavatories is part of the health
administration, it is only proper that the S.M.C. should
provide a certain amount of money for the upkeep of the
public lavatories. It could then prohibit the men who
take charge of these places from compulsorily selling
toilet paper to the public.

our Government to demand the return from the Foreign Powers
of the "gifts" that were never actually extended to them.
The Chinese Government has never extended the right of
factory inspection to the foreign nations, therefore, it
is not only unjustifiable but also unnecessary for China
to negotiate with the foreign nations for the return of
this "gift" (the right of factory inspection).
(2) The collection of income tax: It
seems to be the customary practice of those foreign nations
which have concluded unequal treaties with China to purposely
misrepresent the true legal sense of consular jurisdiction
as a means to refuse observance of whatever Tax Collection
Laws that are promulgated by this country and to oppose
the collection by the local authorities of the various
districts concerned of such taxes as municipal rates, etc.
When the regulations governing the collection of income
tax were promulgated last year, it was quite in the
expectation of our Government that they would meet with
opposition from foreign quarters. As a matter of fact, views
in opposition to the application of these regulations to
foreign subjects have frequently appeared in foreign papers
and magazines published in China. With the exception of
only a very few British and American nationals, who comprise
mostly missionaries, the greater part of the foreign residents
in China are still vigorously opposed to the payment of
this tax to the Chinese Government. From this, we can see
quite clearly that this question will unquestionably be the
most difficult for solution of all Sino-Foreign problems.
It is the right of the Chinese Government to
collect income tax; there is no legal basis for the foreign
nations to express their opposition to this collection. It
is most ridiculous and absurd for the foreign nations to take
advantage of the existence of consular jurisdiction as a
screen for their opposition. There is absolutely no connection
whatsoever between consular jurisdiction and the duty of the
foreign residents in China to pay taxes to the Chinese
Government. This can be verified by a study of the provisions
of the existing treaties.
Ostensibly factory inspection and the
collection of income tax are two different matters, but they
are similar to each other in nature in the following points:-
(1) Both of these systems have already been
in force and existence in European and American states for
a considerable number of years; China only follows the
footsteps of the European and American nations and is not the
only country where such systems are introduced. Therefore,
no object should arise to the enforcement of these two
matters merely because of the difference in customs between
Chinese and western peoples.
(2) These two measures are to be enforced
throughout the country and are applicable to all peoples
irrespective of nationalities. It is not for the purpose of
dealing with the foreign residents in China alone that they
are introduced.
(3) These two systems are introduced for
mutual benefit. The enforcement of factory inspection can
bring about proper development of industry, beneficial to
both capitalists and workers, while the collection of income
tax will enable the Chinese Government to acquire stable
revenue, thereby enabling it to consolidate its foundation
for national reconstruction and development, which will in
turn bring about the development of foreign trade with China.

我国政府要求外国列强归还从未实际给予他们的“礼物”。中国政府从未将工厂检查权授予外国列强，因此，中国与外国列强谈判归还这一“礼物”（工厂检查权）不仅没有理由，而且没有必要。
(2) 所得税征收：似乎那些与中国签订不平等条约的外国列强的惯常做法是，故意歪曲领事裁判权的真正法律含义，以此作为拒绝遵守本国颁布的任何税法的手段，并反对有关地区地方当局征收市政捐等税款。去年所得税征收条例颁布时，我国政府预料到会遇到外国方面的反对。事实上，在中国出版的外文报刊上经常出现反对将这些条例适用于外国人的观点。除极少数主要是传教士的英美国民外，在华外国居民的大部分人仍然强烈反对向中国政府缴纳此税。由此可见，这个问题无疑将是所有中外问题中最难解决的。
征收所得税是中国政府的权利；外国列强反对此项征收没有法律依据。外国列强利用领事裁判权的存在作为其反对的掩护，这是极其荒谬和可笑的。领事裁判权与在华外国居民向中国政府纳税的义务之间绝对没有任何联系。这一点可以通过研究现行条约的条款得到证实。
表面上看，工厂检查和所得税征收是两件不同的事情，但它们在性质上有以下相似之处：
(1) 这两种制度在欧美国家已经实行存在了相当长的时间；中国只是追随欧美国家的脚步，并非唯一引入此类制度的国家。因此，仅仅因为中西风俗习惯的差异，就不应对实施这两项事务提出反对。
(2) 这两项措施将在全国范围内实施，适用于所有民族的人民。其引入目的并非仅为了对付在华外国居民。
(3) 引入这两种制度是为了互利。实施工厂检查可以促进工业的适当发展，对资本家和工人都有利，而征收所得税将使中国政府获得稳定的收入，从而使其能够巩固国家重建和发展的基础，进而促进对华贸易的发展。

China by foreigners. It was not until the 12th Year
(1923) of the Chinese Republic that a set of Provisional
Measures Governing Factories was promulgated by the Ministry
of Industry and Commerce of the now defunct Peking Government.
Though they were not enforced at that time, they were,
however, considered unacceptable by the authorities of the

Subsequent to its establishment, the
National Government has been paying special attention to
the welfare and interests of workers and was able to
promulgate, after repeated revisions, the Regulations
Governing the Inspection of Factories in the 20th Year
(1931) of the Chinese Republic, and the Revised Factory
Act as well as the Regulations Governing Its Enforcement,
in the 21st Year. Following the promulgation of these
measures, the authorities of the Foreign Settlements in
Shanghai at once declared that the factories located inside
the limits of the Foreign Settlements were not to be subject
to inspection by the Chinese authorities. As a result of
repeated energetic negotiations, which took about five
years, between Mr. O.K. Yui, then Chief Secretary of the
Shanghai City Government, and Mr. S. Fessenden, Secretary-
General of the S.M.C., a draft agreement over this question
was drawn up on June 24 last year. However, it was
subsequently turned down by the Consular Body when it was
submitted for their endorsement. For this reason, the
question has remained outstanding.
In rejecting the draft agreement, the
Consular Body stated that this agreement could only be
applicable to those factories established inside the
Settlement by Chinese but not to foreign-owned factories,
the inspection of which by the Chinese authorities would
mean a deprivation of privileges allowed in the existing
treaties to those foreigners who enjoy extraterritoriality
or consular jurisdiction. The Consular Body also declared
that the S.M.C. has no right to make any concessions to the
Chinese authorities in connection with this problem because
it is a question between the Chinese Government and the
various Foreign Powers concerned. What a misleading
statement this is! The term used by the Consular Body to
the effect that the S.M.C. has no right to make concessions
to the Chinese authorities,..., when explained from a
legal point of view, means really that the S.M.C. has no
right to prevent the Chinese authorities from conducting
factory inspection inside the Settlement. There can never
arise in this controversy the question of making concessions
or not. If this be the case, then it is only the Chinese
authorities which are offering concessions to the S.M.C.,
as they are compelled to negotiate with the S.M.C. over
this question because of the existing circumstances. It
seems that the Consular Body, when declaring that factory
inspection is a question between the Chinese Government and
the various Foreign Powers concerned, was suspicious of
the attitude of the National Government because the latter
had charged the Shanghai City Government with this task
instead of resorting to negotiations through proper diplomatic
channels. It should not be overlooked that there was some
hidden contempt and meaning in this expression.

国民政府成立后，一直特别关注工人的福利和利益，经过多次修订，得以在中华民国二十年（1931年）颁布《工厂检查法》，并在二十一年颁布《修正工厂法》及其施行条例。在这些措施颁布后，上海外国租界当局立即宣布，位于外国租界范围内的工厂不受中国当局的检查。经过约五年的反复积极谈判，时任上海市政府秘书长的俞鸿钧（O.K. Yui）先生与工部局总办费信惇（S. Fessenden）先生于去年6月24日就此问题起草了一份协议草案。然而，该草案随后在提交领事团认可时被驳回。因此，该问题仍未解决。
领事团在驳回协议草案时声称，该协议仅适用于由中国人在租界内设立的工厂，而不适用于外资工厂，中国当局对外资工厂的检查意味着剥夺现行条约赋予享有治外法权或领事裁判权的那些外国人的特权。领事团还宣称，工部局无权在此问题上向中国当局做出任何让步，因为这是中国政府与各相关外国列强之间的问题。这是多么误导性的陈述啊！领事团使用的措辞，即工部局无权向中国当局做出让步……，从法律角度解释，实际上意味着工部局无权阻止中国当局在租界内进行工厂检查。在这场争议中，根本不存在是否做出让步的问题。如果是这样，那么只有中国当局在向工部局做出让步，因为他们由于现有情况被迫就此问题与工部局进行谈判。看来，领事团在宣称工厂检查是中国政府与各相关外国列强之间的问题时，是对国民政府的态度表示怀疑，因为后者将此任务交给上海市政府，而不是通过适当的外交渠道进行谈判。不应忽视这种表述中包含着某种隐藏的轻蔑和意味。

May 19, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

The "Eastern Miscellany" ( 東方雜誌 ), a fortnightly, Volume 34, Issue No. 10, published on May 16 the following article written by one Sih Tih-tseng ( 施迪曾 ) :-

SOME LEGAL ASPECTS OF THE QUESTION OF CONSULAR JURISDICTION

Before proceeding, I have to point out herewith that this article was written not for the purpose of dealing with the question as to whether or not the consular jurisdiction enjoyed by the various Foreign Powers in China should be abolished but for the purpose of studying from a legal aspect the meaning of consular jurisdiction.

Following the attainment of this special privilege in China by the various Foreign Powers, China was placed in a very unequal position. Not content with their enjoyment of this privilege in China, the Powers have always deliberately misinterpreted the meaning of consular jurisdiction despite its legal aspects, thereby causing China to suffer more loss of her sovereign rights. That the consular jurisdiction enjoyed by the various Foreign Powers in China should be abolished is true, but it should not be overlooked that following the abolition of this system, the Powers can still apply to the provisions of the existing treaties as a means of shelter. China should, however, strongly denounce any improper tendencies that the Foreign Powers may have to attain unreasonable privileges in China by means of deliberate misinterpretation of the meaning of the term: "consular jurisdiction" without due consideration of the legal aspects of this question. In view of the fact that the reasons given by the foreign nations sound quite reasonable and seem at first to be full of legal justification, the Chinese authorities, if they are ignorant of the legal aspects of this question, are very likely to be led astray.

Recently, the foreigners (referring to those who enjoy consular jurisdiction in China), under the pretext of the existence of consular jurisdiction, have refused to observe the Chinese laws for the enforcement of factory inspection and the collection of income tax. They remain persistent in their attitude and continue to misinterpret the meaning of the term: "consular jurisdiction" despite the denouncement and criticisms of the Chinese Government. The Chinese populace, without first carefully studying the problem, likewise consider that the views of the Foreign Powers have a legal basis. For this reason, it seems necessary that a study should be made as to the exact legal meaning of consular jurisdiction.

It should be noted that consular jurisdiction was only extended to the foreign nations in China in those matters which are related to the judicial system of this country, but do not affect the legislative and administrative rights of China, which are still independent.

双周刊《东方杂志》第三十四卷第十期，于5月16日刊载了施迪曾（Sih Tih-tseng）所写的一篇文章：——

领事裁判权问题的若干法律层面

在开始之前，我必须指出，撰写本文的目的并非为了处理是否应废除各外国列强在中国享有的领事裁判权这一问题，而是旨在从法律角度研究领事裁判权的含义。

自从各外国列强在中国获得这一特权后，中国便处于极不平等的地位。列强并不满足于仅在中国享有此特权，尽管从法律层面来看，他们一直故意曲解领事裁判权的含义，从而导致中国遭受更多主权损失。各外国列强在中国享有的领事裁判权确实应当废除，但不应忽视的是，在该制度废除后，列强仍可援引现行条约条款作为庇护手段。然而，中国应强烈谴责任何不当倾向，即外国列强在不充分考虑该问题法律层面的情况下，通过故意曲解“领事裁判权”一词的含义，以获取在中国的不合理特权。鉴于外国提出的理由听起来相当合理，且初看似乎具有充分的法律依据，如果中国当局不了解该问题的法律层面，就很容易被引入歧途。

最近，外国人（指那些在中国享有领事裁判权的人）以存在领事裁判权为借口，拒绝遵守中国关于实施工厂检查和征收所得税的法律。尽管中国政府予以谴责和批评，他们仍坚持其态度，并继续曲解“领事裁判权”一词的含义。中国民众在未仔细研究该问题之前，同样认为外国列强的观点具有法律依据。因此，似乎有必要对领事裁判权的确切法律含义进行研究。

应当注意，领事裁判权仅延伸至外国列强在中国涉及该国司法制度的事务中，但并不影响中国仍然独立的立法权和行政权。

Chinese Courts
Here Said Not
Closing Doors

Tribunals’ Existence
Guaranteed By Treaty
Agreements

Despite current reports to the contrary, Chinese courts in the International Settlement and French Concession will continue to operate, it was learned yesterday.

Since the courts were created by treaty arrangements between China and the Consular body and French authorities here, their existence can be terminated only by mutual agreements, authoritative quarters informed THE CHINA PRESS yesterday.

The agreement creating the Courts in the International Settlement, signed on February 17, 1930, by China and the Consular body was put into operation for three years.

Before its expiration, however, the agreement was given a new lease of life for three more years, with the added provision that at the end of that period, the agreement would continue to run unless a six-month notice is given by one party signifying its intention to terminate the arrangement.

A similar agreement, concluded between China and the French authorities in July, 1931, brought the Chinese courts in the French Concession into existence.

In 1934 when the agreement was due to expire, the same arrangement for extension was agreed upon between the Chinese and French authorities as between the Chinese and the Consular body a year ago.

Chinese courts now existing in Shanghai are the Second High Court, the Third High Court, the First Special District Court and the Second Special District Court.

尽管目前有相反报道，但据悉，国际公共租界和法租界内的中国法院将继续运作。

权威人士昨日向《字林西报》透露，由于这些法院是依据中国与领事团及当地法国当局之间的条约安排设立的，其存续只能通过双方协议终止。

中国与领事团于1930年2月17日签署的设立国际公共租界法院的协议，有效期为三年。

然而，在期满之前，该协议又续期三年，并增加规定：在该期限结束时，除非一方发出六个月的通知表明其终止安排的意向，否则协议将继续有效。

中国与法国当局于1931年7月达成的一项类似协议，促成了法租界内中国法院的设立。

1934年，当该协议即将到期时，中法当局之间达成了与一年前中国与领事团之间相同的延期安排。

目前存在于上海的中国法院包括：江苏高等法院第二分院、江苏高等法院第三分院、上海第一特区地方法院和第二特区地方法院。

March 31, 1939. Morning Translation

Eastern Times and other local newspapers :-

COURT RENDITION AGREEMENT TO CONTINUE

The International Settlement Court Rendition Agreement, which was concluded on February 17, 1930 between China, on one side, and Great Britain, America, France, Brazil and Norway, on the other, will expire on March 31. According to the stipulations of the agreement, any party desiring to cancel the agreement should notify the other party of such intention six months prior to the expiration of the agreement, otherwise the agreement will continue to be in force. As the National Government and the Consular Body have not issued any notification cancelling the agreement, it will continue to be in force even after the date of its expiry.

FILE

On and after April 1 all the decisions of the Shanghai First Special District Court will continue to be upheld by the agreement and the status quo will be strictly maintained. Strict precautionary measures in guarding the Court are being adopted by British soldiers stationed at the place.

Standard (brief comment) :-

The International Settlement Court Rendition Agreement, which has been in force for nine years, will expire on March 31. According to the last paragraph of Article 10 of the agreement, if both parties to the agreement fail to give notice of cancellation six months prior to the expiry of the agreement, it will be regarded as having been extended.

SHANGHAI TIMES.
APR 2 1939
Extra Guards
Placed Over
Local Court
Fear Of Disturbances
Following Statement
Of Mayor Fu
SEARCH OF PERSONS
ENTERING GROUND
Unusual precautions were
taken at the Shanghai First
Special District Court yester-
day morning, when British
military sentries with fixed
bayonets were posted at the
entrance to the judiciary and a
search party of Chinese con-
stables, under a foreign officer,
examined and interrogated all
persons entering the court pre-
cincts.
The presence of the British sen-
tries is not a complete innovation,
as an armed detachment was station-
ed at the court during the critical
period of the recent hostilities. Their
presence yesterday was merely an-
other precautionary measure taken
in case reactionary elements at-
tempted to create a disturbance in
support of the Reformed Govern-
ment, following the announcement
made a few days ago by Mayor Fu
Siao-en regarding the future status
of the Special District Courts in the
Settlement and the French Conces-
sion.
But the search party at the court
entrance was a new departure. All
persons seeking entry to the build-
ings were first subjected to a close
scrutiny, a search and an interro-
gation. If they satisfied the search
party that their presence was re-
quired inside the court grounds
they were permitted to enter.
Reason For Precautions
The underlying motive for this
procedure, it was pointed out by
officials of the Court, lay in the
fact that, from April 1, judgments
of the Court would not be held
legal and the status of the Court
would not be recognized by the Re-
formed Government at Nanking.
This announcement was contained
in the most recent communication
by Mayor Fu of the Reformed Gov-
ernment to the Shanghai Municipal
Council and the Consular Body.
The Shanghai First Special Dis-
trict Court, although within the
Settlement and the British Defence
Sector, is regarded as Chinese ter-
ritory by the S.M.C. It has the
same status as the Chinese Post
Office. In view of this fact and the
assertion of the Reformed Govern-
ment regarding its future status it
was feared in some circles that an
attempt might be made to interfere
with the functioning of the Court,
and certain precautions were deem-
ed advisable.
Fortunately, nothing of an unto-
ward character occurred yesterday.

1939年4月2日
增派警卫
看守本地法院
傅市长声明后
担心发生骚乱
搜查进入场地的人员
昨天上午，上海第一特区地方法院采取了不同寻常的预防措施，持固定刺刀的英国军事哨兵被部署在司法机构入口处，由一名外籍警官率领的中国巡捕搜查队对所有进入法院辖区的人员进行检查和盘问。
英国哨兵的出现并非完全的新举措，因为在最近的敌对行动关键时期，有一支武装分队驻扎在法院。昨天的出现仅仅是另一种预防措施，以防反动分子在傅筱庵（Fu Siao-en）市长几天前宣布关于租界和法租界特区地方法院未来地位之后，试图制造骚乱以支持维新政府。
但是，法院入口处的搜查队是一个新举措。所有寻求进入大楼的人员首先受到严密审查、搜查和盘问。如果他们使搜查队相信他们的存在是法院辖区内所必需的，则允许他们进入。
预防措施的原因
法院官员指出，这一程序的根本动机在于这样一个事实：从4月1日起，法院的判决将不被视为合法，南京维新政府也不承认法院的地位。这一声明包含在维新政府傅市长最近致上海工部局和领事团的函件中。
上海第一特区地方法院虽然位于租界和英军防区内，但被工部局视为中国领土。它具有与中国邮局相同的地位。鉴于这一事实以及维新政府对其未来地位的宣称，某些圈子担心可能会试图干扰法院的运作，因此认为采取某些预防措施是明智的。
幸运的是，昨天没有发生任何不幸事件。

District Court Guarded
By Police, Military
All Entrants Searched;
Incident Feared
British military and the Settlement police authorities were more vigilant than usual in guarding the First Special District Court in North Chekiang Road yesterday, as it was reported that the police had received information that some untoward incident might happen, as the new Chinese city régime in Kiangwan has been demanding the handing over of the tribunal to its control.
Special precautions have been taken by the authorities since the beginning of the month, as it has been asserted by the new régime that the terms of the Court Rendition Agreement expired on April 1. Counteracting the statement, Chinese press reports stated that the terms mentioned in the agreement signed between China and the Powers concerned still hold good, since no revision has been asked for by either side to the contract, which procedure ought to be carried out six months before expiration.
Only lawyers wearing badges and newspapermen armed with documentary proofs were allowed to go into the court freely yesterday, but all other people who wished to enter the gate of the court were carefully searched.

昨天，只有佩戴徽章的律师和持有书面证明的新闻记者才被允许自由进入法院，但所有其他希望进入法院大门的人都受到了仔细搜查。

THE MUNICIPAL GAZETTE, FRIDAY, MARCH 7, 1930. 


Agreement Relating to the Chinese 
Courts in the International Settle- 
ment at Shanghai. 


ARTICLE I. 


From the date on which the pre- 
sent Agreement comes into force, 
all former rules, agreements, ex- 
changes of notes et cetera, having 
special reference to the establish- 
ment of a Chinese court in the 
International Settlement at Shang- 
hai shall be abolished. 


ARTICLE II. 


The Chinese Government shall, in 
accordance with Chinese laws and 
regulations relating to the judiciary 
and subject to the terms of the pre- 
sent Agreement, establish im the 
International Settlement at Shang- 
hai a District Court (Ti Fang Fa 
Yuan) and a Branch High Court 
(Kao Teng Fa Yuan Fen Yuan). 
All Chinese laws and regulations, 
substantive as well as procedural, 
which are now in force, or which 
may hereafter be duly enacted and 
promulgated shall be applicable in 
the Courts, due account »eing taken 
of the Land Regulations and Bye- 
laws of the International Settlement, 
which are applicable pending their 
adoption and promulgation by the 
Chinese Government, and of the 
terms of the present Agreement. 

Judgments, decisions and rulings 
of the Branch High Court are sub- 
ject to appeal, according to Chinese 
law, to the Supreme Court of China. 


Argticir. III. 


The former practice of Consular 
deputies or Consular officials ap- 
pearing to watch proceedings or to 
sit jointly iu the Chinese court now 
functioning in the International 
Settlement shall be discontinued in 
the Courts established under the pre- 
sent Agreement. 


ARTICLE IV. 


When any person is arrested by 
the Municipal or judicial Police, he 
shall, within twenty-four hours, ex- 
clusive of holidays, be sent to the 
Courts established under the present 
Agreement to be dealt with, failing 
which he shall be released. 


ARTICLE V. 


The Courts established under the 
present Agreement shall each have a 
certain number of procurators to be 
appointed by the Chinese Govern- 
ment, who shall hold inquests and 
autopsies (Chien Yen) within the 
jurisdiction of these Courts and 
shall otherwise perform their 
function in accordance with Chinese 
law in all cases involving the ap- 
plication of Articles 103 to 186 of 
the Chinese Criminal Code, except 
where the Municipal Police of the 
International Settlement or the 
party concerned has already initinted 
prosecution, provided that all preli- 
minary investigations conducted by 
the procurator shall be held pub- 
licly and counsel for the accused 
shall have the rigit to be present 
and heard. 

In other cases arising within the 
jurisdiction of the Courts, the Muni- 
cipal Police or the party concerned 
shall prosecute. The  procurator 
shall have the right to express his 


views in court in all criminal cases 
in which the prosecution is initiated 
by the Municipal Police or the party 
concerned. 


ARTICLE VI. 
All judicial processes, such as 
summonses, warrants, orders, ef 


cetera, shall be valid only after they 
have been signed by a judge of the 
Courts established under the present 
Agreement, whereupon they shall be 
served or executed by the judicial 
police or, as provided below, by the 
process-servers thereof. 

No person found in the Interna- 
tional Settlement shall be handed 
over to the extra-Settlement authori- 
ties without a preliminary investiga- 
tion in court at which counsel for 
the accused shall have the right to 
be present and heard, except in the 
case of ts emanating from 
other Modern Law Courts when the 
accused may be handed over after 
his identity has been established by 
the Court. 


All judgments, decisions and 
rulings of the Courts shall be 
executed as soon as they become 
final as a result of the judicial 
procedure in force in the eaid Courts. 
Whenever necessary, the Municipal 
Police shall render any assistance 
within their power as may be re- 
quested of them. 


The process-servers of the Courts 
shall be appointed by the Presidents 
of the Courts respectively and their 
duties shali be to serve all sum- 
monses and deliver other documents 
of the Courts in connection with civil 
cases. For the execution of judg- 
ments in civil cases, the process- 
servers shall be accompanied by the 
judicial police. The officers and 
members of the judicial police of the 
Courts shall be appointed by the 
President of the Branch High Court 
upon the recommendation of the 
Municipal Council and shall be sub- 
ject to dismissal by the President 
of that Court upon cause shown. 
Their services will also be ter- 
minated by the President at the re- 
quest of the Municipal Council upon 
cause shown. They shal! wear the 
uniform designed by the Chinese 
judicial authu:iues, and shall be 
subject to the orders and direction 
of the Courts and faithful to their 
duties. 


ARTICLE VII. 


The House of Detention for civil 
cases and the Women’s Prison 
attached to the Chinese Court now 
functioning in the International 
Settlement at Shanghai shall be 
transferred from that court to the 
Courts established under the pre- 
sent Agreement and shall be super- 
vised and administered by the 
Chinese authorities. 


All prisoners now serving sen- 
tences in the prisons attached to the 
Chinese Court now functioning in 
the International Settlement and 
those sentenced by the Courts 
established under the present Agree- 
ment shall, at the discretion of the 
said Courts, serve their sentences 
either in such prisons in the Settle- 
ment or in Chinese prisons outside 
the Settlement, except that offenders 


against the Police Offences Code 
and the Land Regulations and Bye- 
laws and persons under arrest await- 
ing trial shall serve their periods 
of detention in the Settlement. The 
prisons in the Settlement shall be 
operated, as far as practicable, in 
conformity with Chinese prison re- 
gulations and shall be subject to 
inspection, from time to time, by 
officers appointed by the Chinese 
judicial] authorities. 


Persons sentenced to death by the 
Courts established under the present 
Agreement shall be sent to the 
Chinese authorities outside of the 
Settlement for execution of. such 
sentence. 


Arriciz VIII. 


Foreign lawyers duly qualified will 
be admitted to practice in the Courts 
established under the present Agree- 
ment in all cases in which a 
foreigner is a party, provided such 
foreign lawyer can only represent 
the foreign party concerned. The 
Municipal Council may also be repre- 
sented in the same manner by duly 
qualified lawyers, Chinese or foreign, 
in any proceedings in which the 
Council is complainant or plaintiff 
or the Municipal Police is the 
prosecutor.

THE EVIL BFFLCTS OF CONSULAR JURISDICTION 


Consular jurisdiction means that cases in 
which foreigners are involved are not subject to the 
jurisdiction of the authorities of the country in which 
they are residing. . 

The existence of consular jurisdiction in China 
is partly due to the ignorance and corrupt administration of 
the Manchu Government, but principally to coercion and 
oppression ty the foreign Powers under the pretext that the 
judicial system of China at that time was corrupt and not up 
to date. 

Since the establishment of the National Government 
at Nanking, many improvements have been introduced into the 
judicial system of this country and it is now not far behind 
that existing im other civilized nations. But why is 
consular jurisdiction still in force in this country? 

4s consular jurisdiction is an already 
secured privilege, the foreign Powers will never willingly 
relinquigh it. Its existence not only jeopardizes our 
administrative rights and impairs our judicial system 
put encourages ronins to comit unlawful activities such 
as smuggling and inducing traitorous Chinese to change 
their nationality. We should endeavour to bring about 
the abolition of consular jurisdiction. As the existence 
of consular jurisdiction is based upon the unequal treaties, 
we must first work for the abolition of all these treaties.

March 27, 1937. Morning Translation. 


Shun Pao published the following editorial comment on March 26:- 


ABOLITION OF CONSULAR JURISDICTION 


P 7 The system of Consular Jurisdiction has 
in itself many defects. First, the difference in the 
application of laws. The consular jurisdiction depends 
on the nationality of the defendant, and as the laws of 
various countries are not the same, an act which is considered 
an offence by one Consulate is not so regarded by another. 
In consequence, many cases of a like nature bring different 
decisions. 

Secondly, take the non-jurisdiction of 
a Consular Authority over witnesses and plaintiff of a 
adifferent nationality. If thd witnesses necessary for a 
case are cf a nationality different to that of the defendant, 

the latter's consular authority cannot compel them to apnear 

to give evidence nor can it charge them with perjury if they 
are willing to attend byt give false evidence. 

Thirdly, the difficulty in gathering 
evidence in the c@ése of a foreigner committing an offence 
in the interior of China. when a foreigner commits an 
offence while in the interior, he should be handed over 
to his nearest consular authorities to be dealt with; he 
can be arrested but not ill-treated. By this stipulation, a 
foreigner who commits an offence against public morals or 
who commits an offence of intentional manslaughter while 
journeying in the interior of China, must he handed over 
to his consular authorities in a trading port thousands of 
miles awaye In a place which lacks easy coxmunication, it 
would take a long time to hand over an offender to his 
consular authorities, ¢nd it would be a difficult task to 
gather evidence at the time of hearinge 

Fourthly, the difference between the 
office of a Consul and that of a Judge. The office of a 
Consul is to protect the interests of his citizens. It 
is almost an impossibility to expect a fair judgment from 
him when he is required to try a case in which one of his 
citizens is charged by a citizen of another natione 

In view of the foregoing four defects, the 
system of Consular Jurisdiction should have been abolished 
long ago. 

The existence of Consular Jurisdiction is a 
serious encroachment on China's sovereign rights and is 
liable to afford undesirable foreign nationals a shield 
to carry out their subversive activities in our territory. 
For example, the rampant smuggling and trafficking in noxious 
drugs as well as the existence of a great number of special 
military bodies. Consular Jurisdiction is at the root of 
these evils. ; 

We must support our government in its efforts 
to bring about the abolition of Consular Jurisdiction.

LoGAL ASPECT OF CONSULAR JURISDICTION 


For many years, consular jurisdiction 
has been detrimental to China. A nation-wide appeal for 
the independent abolition of this system has been made 
many times and on numerous occasions our Government has 
consulted on the matter with the various Powers concermed 
but without any result. 

After Dr. Wang Chung-hui took over 
the Foreign Affairs Ministry, people throughout the country 
again urged that decided action be taken to abolish 
independently this system which is andangering the people 
as well as the State. We believe that the new Foreign 
Minister will regard as his first important duty the 
settlement of this question. 

From a legal point of view, the 
existence of consular jurisdiction in China is a violation 
of International Law and Treaties. China should be able 
at any time voluntarily to declare the system null and void. 
According to International Law, the sovereign rights of a 
country include all controlling rights, voth administrative 
and judicial, within its own territory. This sovereignty... 
can only be exercised in a nation's own territory and not 
in that of other nations. The existence of consular 
jurisdictionin China is really an infringement of the law, 
because it places foreign nationals in China beyond the 
control of Chinese Law, this impairing Chinese sovereignty. 
The Powers who enjoy this privilege have extended their 
sovereign rights into Chinese territory; this state of 
affairs is contrary to International Law. 

The system of consular jurisdiction was 
put into effect in China in the year 1858 after the 
conclusion of the Anglo-Chinese and Franco-Chinese Treaties 
at Tientsin. As conditions in China have totally changed 
and Sino-Foreign relations are also different from befcre, 
these treaties should not remain in force. Furthermore, 
the League of Nations and the Nine-Power Peace Pact have 
definitely specified the recognition by various Powers of 
the integrity and independence of Chinese sovereignty and 
territory. This stipulation obviously signifies that China 
is an independent country as defined-in International Law. 
As a rule, after the formation of new agreements, the old 
ones which conflict with the new lese their effectiveness. 
Under the League of Nations and the Nine-Power Peace Pact, 
the Tientsin Treaties should become void and consular 
jurisdiction should have no more legal basis. Consular 
jurisdiction is illegal and China has the right naturally 
to abolish it automatically at any time.
